sentences.zh: = 令狐彰 =

translations.literal: = Linghu Zhang =
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Zhang

sentences.zh: 令狐彰，字伯陽，京兆富平人，其先自敦煌內徙。

translations.literal: Linghu Zhang, styled Boyang, was a man of Fuping in Jingzhao; his ancestors had moved inward from Dunhuang.
translations.idiomatic: Linghu Zhang, courtesy name Boyang, was from Fuping in Jingzhao; his family had originally migrated inward from Dunhuang.

sentences.zh: 父濞，為世善吏。

translations.literal: His father Bi was a capable official for generations.
translations.idiomatic: His father Bi had been a capable official for generations.

sentences.zh: 始，尉范陽，通民家女，生彰。

translations.literal: At first, while serving as commandant of Fanyang, he had relations with a commoner's daughter, who bore Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: While he was first serving as commandant of Fanyang, he had relations with a commoner's daughter, who bore Zhang.

sentences.zh: 罷歸，留彰母所。

translations.literal: When he left office and returned home, he left Zhang's mother where she was.
translations.idiomatic: When he left his post and went home, he left Zhang's mother where she was.

sentences.zh: 既長，誌膽沈果，知書傳大義，射命中。

translations.literal: When he had grown up, he was resolute, bold, steady, and decisive; he understood the great principles in the classics, and his archery always hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Once grown, he was resolute and bold, steady and decisive; he grasped the great principles of the classics, and never missed with the bow.

sentences.zh: 從安祿山，署左衛郎將。

translations.literal: He followed An Lushan and was appointed Left Guard Lieutenant-General.
translations.idiomatic: He followed An Lushan and was appointed lieutenant-general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 與張通儒入長安，又署左街使。

translations.literal: He entered Chang'an with Zhang Tongru and was again appointed Left Street Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Chang'an with Zhang Tongru and was again made commissioner of the Left Street.

sentences.zh: 二京平，走河朔。

translations.literal: When the two capitals were pacified, he fled to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: After the two capitals were recovered, he fled to Hebei.

sentences.zh: 史思明署博、滑二州刺史，屯滑臺。

translations.literal: Shi Siming appointed him governor of Bo and Hua prefectures, and he encamped at Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming made him governor of Bo and Hua and stationed him at Huatai.

sentences.zh: 時中人楊萬定監滑州軍，彰欲以節自顯，募沒人夜度河，悉籍士馬州縣獻款，因萬定以聞。

translations.literal: At the time the eunuch Yang Wanding supervised the Hua army; Zhang wished to display his own merit with a military commission, recruited divers to cross the river by night, registered all soldiers and horses in the prefectures and counties to offer allegiance, and had Wan Ding report it.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Yang Wanding was then supervising the Hua garrison. Zhang wanted to win recognition with a formal commission, so he recruited swimmers to cross the river at night, enrolled soldiers and horses throughout the prefectures and counties in pledges of loyalty, and had Wan Ding report this to the court.

sentences.zh: 肅宗大悅，下書慰勞。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong was greatly pleased and issued an edict of consolation and praise.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong was delighted and sent an edict of praise and encouragement.

sentences.zh: 彰移壁杏園渡，思明疑之，遣薛岌以兵劫彰。

translations.literal: Zhang moved his camp to Xingyuan Ford; Siming grew suspicious and sent Xue Ji with troops to attack Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang shifted his camp to Xingyuan Ford. Siming grew suspicious and sent Xue Ji with troops to seize him.

sentences.zh: 彰諭眾以大誼，皆感附死力，遂破岌兵，潰圍出，以麾下數百入朝，賜甲第、帷帳、什器，拜滑亳、魏博節度使。

translations.literal: Zhang addressed the troops on the great cause; all were moved and attached themselves to fight to the death, then broke Ji's army, burst through the encirclement, entered court with several hundred followers, was granted a fine mansion, curtains, and furnishings, and was appointed military commissioner of Hua-Bo and Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang rallied his men with an appeal to the greater cause; they were moved to fight to the death, routed Ji's force, broke out of the siege, and entered court with several hundred followers. He was given a fine mansion, hangings, and furnishings, and appointed military commissioner of Hua-Bo and Weibo.

sentences.zh: 河朔平，加兼御史大夫，封霍國公，檢校尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: When Hebei was pacified, he was additionally made Censor-in-Chief, enfeoffed as Duke of Huo, and appointed acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Hebei was pacified, he was further made censor-in-chief, enfeoffed as Duke of Huo, and appointed acting right vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 始，滑當寇沖，城邑墟榛，彰躬訓吏下，檢軍力農，法令嚴，無敢犯者。

translations.literal: At first Hua lay on the route of invasions; towns and cities were ruins overgrown with brush. Zhang personally trained officials and subordinates, inspected the army and promoted agriculture; the laws were strict and none dared violate them.
translations.idiomatic: Hua had lain in the path of invaders, and its towns were ruined and overgrown. Zhang personally drilled his officials and troops, inspected the army, and promoted farming; his laws were strict, and no one dared break them.

sentences.zh: 田疇大辟，庫委豐余，歲時貢賦如期。

translations.literal: Fields were greatly opened, storehouses were full and abundant, and seasonal tribute and levies arrived on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Fields were widely reclaimed, the treasuries overflowed, and tribute and levies arrived on time each year.

sentences.zh: 時吐蕃盜邊，召防秋兵，彰遣士三千，自賫糧，所過無秋毫犯，供擬讓不受，時韙其能。

translations.literal: At the time the Tibetans raided the borders and autumn-defense troops were summoned; Zhang sent three thousand soldiers who carried their own provisions, harmed not a hair where they passed, and declined supplies offered them; the age praised his ability.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibetans raided the frontier and autumn-defense troops were called up, Zhang sent three thousand men who carried their own rations, took nothing from the people along the way, and refused provisions offered them; contemporaries praised his efficiency.

sentences.zh: 然猜阻忮忍，忤者輒死。

translations.literal: Yet he was suspicious, obstructive, jealous, and cruel; those who crossed him were promptly killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was suspicious, obstructive, jealous, and cruel; anyone who crossed him was killed at once.

sentences.zh: 怒潁州刺史李岵，遣姚奭代之，戒曰：「不時代，殺之。

translations.literal: Angered at Yingzhou prefect Li Qiu, he sent Yao Shi to replace him, warning: "If he does not leave his post in time, kill him."
translations.idiomatic: Angered at Yingzhou prefect Li Qiu, he sent Yao Shi to replace him with orders: "If he does not leave his post in time, kill him."

sentences.zh: 」岵知其謀，因殺奭，死者百餘人，奔汴州，上書自言，彰亦劾之。

translations.literal: Qiu learned of the plot, killed Shi in turn, and more than a hundred died; he fled to Bianzhou, submitted a memorial explaining himself, and Zhang also impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu learned of the plot, killed Shi in turn—more than a hundred died in the affair—fled to Bianzhou, and submitted a memorial in his own defense; Zhang also impeached him.

sentences.zh: 河南尹張延賞畏彰，留岵使，故彰書先聞，斥岵夷州，殺之。

translations.literal: Henan intendant Zhang Yanshang feared Zhang and kept Qiu in his service, so Zhang's memorial arrived first; Qiu was banished to Yizhou and killed.
translations.idiomatic: Henan intendant Zhang Yanshang feared Linghu Zhang and kept Qiu in his service, so Zhang's memorial reached the court first; Qiu was exiled to Yizhou and executed.

sentences.zh: 與魚朝恩有隙，及用事，彰不敢入朝。

translations.literal: He had a rift with Yu Chao'en; when Yu came to power, Zhang did not dare enter court.
translations.idiomatic: He had fallen out with Yu Chao'en; once Yu held power, Zhang no longer dared come to court.

sentences.zh: 會母喪，失明，卒。

translations.literal: When his mother's mourning came, he lost his sight and died.
translations.idiomatic: During his mother's mourning he went blind and died.

sentences.zh: 方疾甚，敕子建、通、運歸東都私第，悉上軍府兵仗財用簿最，表吏部尚書劉晏、工部尚書李勉堪大事，請以自代。

translations.literal: When his illness was severe, he ordered his sons Jian, Tong, and Yun to return to their private residence in the Eastern Capital, submitted complete registers of the military headquarters' arms and finances, and memorialized that Minister of Personnel Liu Yan and Minister of Works Li Mian were fit for great affairs, asking that they replace him.
translations.idiomatic: As his illness worsened, he ordered his sons Jian, Tong, and Yun back to their family residence in Luoyang, turned in full inventories of the headquarters' arms and finances, and recommended Ministers Liu Yan and Li Mian as fit to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 代宗得表咨悼，下詔褒美其門閭，贈太傅。

translations.literal: Emperor Daizong received the memorial and mourned; he issued an edict praising Zhang's house and posthumously appointed him Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daizong received the memorial with grief, issued an edict praising his household, and posthumously made him Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 建累官右龍武軍使。

translations.literal: Jian rose through offices to commissioner of the Right Dragon Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: Jian rose to become commissioner of the Right Dragon Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 德宗幸奉天，建方肄士射，遂以四百人從，且殿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Dezong went to Fengtian, Jian was drilling troops in archery; he followed with four hundred men and served as rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Dezong fled to Fengtian, Jian was drilling his men in archery; he followed with four hundred troops and served as rearguard.

sentences.zh: 擢行在中軍鼓角使、左神武軍大將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to drum-and-horn commissioner of the traveling central army and great general of the Left Divine Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to drum-and-horn commissioner of the traveling central army and great general of the Left Divine Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 其妻，成德節度使李寶臣女也，建將棄之，誣與門下客郭士倫通，榜殺士倫而逐其妻，士倫母痛憤卒。

translations.literal: His wife was the daughter of Chengde military commissioner Li Baochen; Jian was about to abandon her, falsely charged her with having relations with his retainer Guo Shilun, had Shilun beaten to death and drove out his wife; Shilun's mother died of grief and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was the daughter of Chengde commissioner Li Baochen. Jian meant to cast her off, falsely accused her of an affair with his retainer Guo Shilun, had Shilun beaten to death and drove out his wife; Shilun's mother died of grief and outrage.

sentences.zh: 寶臣請劾按，無狀。

translations.literal: Baochen requested investigation and prosecution; no evidence was found.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen demanded an investigation; nothing was proved.

sentences.zh: 建會赦免。

translations.literal: Jian was pardoned in a general amnesty.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was pardoned in a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 帝取常膳錢五十萬葬士倫母子，並恤其家。

translations.literal: The emperor took five hundred thousand in regular meal funds to bury Shilun and his mother and also provided relief to the family.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor drew five hundred thousand cash from his regular meal allowance to bury Shilun and his mother and provided for the family.

sentences.zh: 俄起建為右領軍大將軍。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Jian was raised to great general of the Right Leading Army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Jian was appointed great general of the Right Leading Army.

sentences.zh: 復坐專殺，以勛被貸。

translations.literal: He again was convicted of unauthorized killing but was pardoned for his merit.
translations.idiomatic: He was again convicted of unauthorized killing but was spared because of his service.

sentences.zh: 坐妄自陳，貶施州別駕，卒，贈右領軍大將軍，又加贈揚州大都督。

translations.literal: For making false statements on his own behalf he was demoted to vice-prefect of Shi prefecture and died; he was posthumously given the title of great general of the Right Leading Army, and later also made posthumous Governor-General of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For making false claims on his own behalf he was demoted to vice-prefect of Shi and died there; he was posthumously made great general of the Right Leading Army, and later also governor-general of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 憲宗時，宰相李吉甫奏言：「彰將死，籍上土地兵甲，遣諸子還第，彰同時河朔諸鎮，傳子孫，熏灼數代，唯彰忠義奮發，而長子建坐事，幼子運無辜，皆竄死，今通幸存，惟陛下用之。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xianzong's time, Chief Minister Li Jifu memorialized: "When Zhang was about to die, he registered and submitted the land and arms, sent his sons back to their residence; among the Hebei garrisons of his day, power passed to sons and grandsons and blazed for generations—only Zhang rose in loyal righteousness, yet his eldest son Jian was implicated in a case, his youngest son Yun died innocent, both exiled to death; now Tong alone survives—may Your Majesty employ him."
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianzong, Chief Minister Li Jifu wrote: "As Zhang lay dying, he turned in inventories of land and arms and sent his sons home. Among the Hebei warlords of his day, power passed through families for generations—only Zhang acted in loyal devotion. Yet his eldest son Jian was implicated in a crime, and his youngest Yun died in exile though innocent. Tong alone survives; I beg Your Majesty to employ him."

sentences.zh: 」因授贊善大夫。

translations.literal: He was accordingly appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Tong was accordingly appointed attendant of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 時討蔡，故連徙壽州團練使。

translations.literal: At the time they were campaigning against Cai, so he was repeatedly transferred and made regimental commissioner of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because the court was campaigning against Cai, he was moved in succession to regimental commissioner of Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 聞吉甫卒，不自安。

translations.literal: When he heard that Jifu had died, he felt ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned of Jifu's death, he grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 每戰，虛張首級，敗則掩不奏。

translations.literal: In every battle he inflated the count of heads; when defeated he concealed it and did not report.
translations.idiomatic: In every battle he inflated enemy casualties; when he lost, he hid it and filed no report.

sentences.zh: 露布上，宰相武元衡卻之。

translations.literal: When victory bulletins were submitted, Chief Minister Wu Yuanheng returned them.
translations.idiomatic: When his victory bulletins reached the court, Chief Minister Wu Yuanheng sent them back.

sentences.zh: 後為賊攻，焚廥聚，破屯柵，通大懼，重塹不敢出。

translations.literal: Later he was attacked by bandits who burned the granaries and broke the stockades; Tong was greatly afraid, dug deeper moats, and did not dare go out.
translations.idiomatic: Later rebels attacked him, burned his granaries, and broke his stockades; Tong was terrified, dug deeper ditches, and would not venture out.

sentences.zh: 詔金吾大將軍李文通宣慰，將至，遂代之。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Golden Guard great general Li Wentong as pacification commissioner; before he arrived, Tong was replaced.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Golden Guard great general Li Wentong as pacification commissioner; before Li arrived, Tong was removed.

sentences.zh: 貶昭州司戶參軍事。

translations.literal: He was demoted to revenue adjutant of Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to revenue adjutant of Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 久乃召為右衛將軍，給事中崔植還其制，帝使喻植，以彰有功，不忍棄其嗣，制乃下。

translations.literal: After a long time he was summoned as general of the Right Guard; Attendant Cui Zhi returned his appointment edict; the emperor had someone explain to Zhi that because Zhang had merit, he could not bear to abandon his descendant, and the edict was then issued.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was recalled as general of the Right Guard. Attendant Cui Zhi returned his appointment edict, but the emperor explained that Zhang's service made him unwilling to abandon his line; the edict was then issued.

sentences.zh: 終左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He ended as great general of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as great general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 運為東都留守將，為杜亞所陷，流死歸州。

translations.literal: Yun was a general of the Eastern Capital garrison; framed by Du Ya, he was exiled and died in Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yun served as a general of the Luoyang garrison; framed by Du Ya, he was exiled and died in Guizhou.

sentences.zh: = 張孝忠 =

translations.literal: = Zhang Xiaozhong =
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiaozhong

sentences.zh: 張孝忠，字孝忠，本奚種，世為乙失活酋長。

translations.literal: Zhang Xiaozhong, styled Xiaozhong, was originally of Xi stock; for generations his family were chiefs of Yiwenhuo.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiaozhong, courtesy name Xiaozhong, was of Xi descent; his family had been chiefs of the Yiwenhuo tribe for generations.

sentences.zh: 父謐，開元中提眾納款，授鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: His father Mi in the Kaiyuan era led his following in submission and was appointed Chamberlain for Dependencies.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mi led his people in submission during the Kaiyuan era and was made chamberlain for dependencies.

sentences.zh: 孝忠始名阿勞，以勇聞，燕、趙間共推張阿勞、王沒諾幹，二人齊名。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong was originally named Alao; famed for courage, between Yan and Zhao they jointly acclaimed Zhang Alao and Wang Meinuogan as equally renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong was originally called Alao. Renowned for bravery, people across Yan and Zhao ranked Zhang Alao and Wang Meinuogan as equals in fame.

sentences.zh: 沒諾幹，王武俊也。

translations.literal: Meinuogan was Wang Wujun.
translations.idiomatic: Meinuogan was Wang Wujun.

sentences.zh: 孝忠魁偉，長六尺，性寬裕，事親孝。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong was imposing in stature, six feet tall, generous in nature, and filial toward his parents.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong was imposing, six feet tall, open-handed by nature, and devoted to his parents.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，以善射供奉仗內。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianbao era, for skill in archery he served in attendance within the imperial guard.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Tianbao era his archery won him a place on the emperor's personal guard.

sentences.zh: 安祿山奏為偏將，破九姓突厥，以功擢漳源府折沖。

translations.literal: An Lushan recommended him as deputy general; he defeated the Nine Surname Turks and for merit was promoted to commander of Zhangyuan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: An Lushan recommended him as a deputy general. He defeated the Nine Surname Turks and was promoted to commander of Zhangyuan for his merit.

sentences.zh: 祿山、史思明陷河、洛，常為賊前鋒。

translations.literal: When Lushan and Shi Siming took the Yellow River region and Luoyang, he often served as the rebels' vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When Lushan and Shi Siming seized the Yellow River basin and Luoyang, he often led the rebel vanguard.

sentences.zh: 朝義敗，乃自歸，授左領軍將軍，以兵屬李寶臣。

translations.literal: When Chaoyi was defeated, he returned on his own, was appointed general of the Left Leading Army, and his troops were placed under Li Baochen.
translations.idiomatic: After Chaoyi's defeat he came over on his own, was made general of the Left Leading Army, and his troops were assigned to Li Baochen.

sentences.zh: 累加左金吾衛將軍，賜今名。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to general of the Left Golden Guard and granted his present name.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to general of the Left Golden Guard and was granted his present name.

sentences.zh: 寶臣以其沈毅謹詳，遂為姻家，易州諸屯委以統制，十餘年，威惠流聞。

translations.literal: Baochen, for his steadiness, firmness, prudence, and thoroughness, made him a son-in-law by marriage and entrusted him with command over the garrisons of Yizhou; for more than ten years his authority and kindness spread in renown.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen admired his steadiness and prudence, married into his family, and put him in charge of the Yizhou garrisons; for more than ten years his authority and kindness were widely known.

sentences.zh: 田承嗣寇冀州，寶臣付兵四千，使出上谷，屯貝丘。

translations.literal: Tian Chengsi raided Jizhou; Baochen gave him four thousand troops and sent him out through Shanggu to encamp at Beiqiu.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Chengsi raided Jizhou, Baochen gave Xiaozhong four thousand men and sent him out through Shanggu to camp at Beiqiu.

sentences.zh: 承嗣見其軍整嚴，嘆曰：「阿勞在焉，冀未可圖也。

translations.literal: Chengsi saw his army orderly and strict and sighed: "With Alao there, Jizhou cannot yet be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi saw how disciplined his army was and sighed, "With Alao there, Jizhou cannot be taken yet."

sentences.zh: 」即焚營去。

translations.literal: He immediately burned his camp and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He burned his camp and withdrew at once.

sentences.zh: 寶臣與朱滔戰瓦橋，奏孝忠為易州刺史，分精騎七千，當幽州。

translations.literal: Baochen fought Zhu Tao at Waqiao, memorialized to make Xiaozhong prefect of Yizhou, and assigned him seven thousand elite cavalry to face Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Baochen fought Zhu Tao at Waqiao, he had Xiaozhong appointed prefect of Yizhou and gave him seven thousand elite cavalry to hold the line against Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 擢太子賓客，封符陽郡王。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Guest of the Heir Apparent and enfeoffed as Prince of Fuyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to guest of the heir apparent and enfeoffed as Prince of Fuyang.

sentences.zh: 寶臣晚節稍忌刻，殺大將李獻誠等而召孝忠，孝忠不往，復使其弟孝節召之。

translations.literal: In his later years Baochen grew somewhat jealous and harsh; he killed great generals such as Li Xiancheng and summoned Xiaozhong, who did not come; he again sent his younger brother Xiaojie to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Baochen grew jealous and harsh, killed senior generals including Li Xiancheng, and summoned Xiaozhong, who refused to come; he then sent his brother Xiaojie.

sentences.zh: 孝忠復命曰：「諸將無狀，連頸受戮。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong replied: "The generals have been guilty of nothing yet are executed one after another with their necks linked."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong replied, "The generals have done nothing wrong, yet they are executed in batches."

sentences.zh: 吾懼禍，不敢往，亦不敢叛，猶公不覲天子也。

translations.literal: "I fear disaster and dare not go, yet I also dare not rebel—just as you, sir, have not gone to audience with the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: "I fear for my life and dare not come, yet I dare not rebel either—just as you yourself have not gone to court."

sentences.zh: 」孝節泣曰：「即歸，且僇死。

translations.literal: Xiaojie wept and said: "If I return now, I shall be put to death at once."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaojie wept and said, "If I go back now, I will be killed at once."

sentences.zh: 」孝忠曰：「偕往則並命，吾留，無患也。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong said: "If we go together we shall both die; if I stay, there will be no trouble."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong said, "If we go together we both die; if I stay, you will be safe."

sentences.zh: 」果不敢殺。

translations.literal: In the end he did not dare kill him.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Baochen did not dare kill him.

sentences.zh: 然寶臣素善孝忠，及病不能語，以手指北而死。

translations.literal: Yet Baochen had always been on good terms with Xiaozhong; when ill and unable to speak, he pointed north with his finger and died.
translations.idiomatic: Baochen had always favored Xiaozhong; when he fell ill and could no longer speak, he pointed north and died.

sentences.zh: 子惟嶽擅立，詔朱滔以幽州兵討之。

translations.literal: His son Weiyue seized power on his own; an edict ordered Zhu Tao to campaign against him with Youzhou troops.
translations.idiomatic: His son Weiyue seized power on his own; the court ordered Zhu Tao to campaign against him with Youzhou troops.

sentences.zh: 滔忌孝忠善戰，慮師出為己患，使判官蔡雄往說曰：「惟嶽孺子，弄兵拒命，吾奉詔伐罪，公乃宿將，安用助逆而不自求福也？

translations.literal: Tao, jealous of Xiaozhong's skill in battle and fearing that if troops marched out they would become a threat to himself, sent his aide Cai Xiong to persuade him, saying: "Weiyue is a mere boy who plays with arms and defies orders; I campaign by edict to punish crime—you are a veteran general; why aid the rebel and not seek fortune for yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: Tao, jealous of Xiaozhong's fighting ability and fearing that an expedition would create a rival, sent his aide Cai Xiong to persuade him: "Weiyue is a boy playing at rebellion; I march under imperial orders to punish him. You are a veteran—why aid a rebel instead of winning favor for yourself?"

sentences.zh: 今昭義、河東軍已破田悅，而淮西軍下襄陽，梁崇義屍出井中，斬漢江上者五千人，河南軍計日北首，趙、魏滅亡可見。

translations.literal: Now the Zhaoyi and Hedong armies have already defeated Tian Yue, while the Huaixi army has descended on Xiangyang; Liang Chongyi's corpse was taken from a well, five thousand were beheaded on the Han River, the Henan army will turn north within days—the destruction of Zhao and Wei can be seen.
translations.idiomatic: "The Zhaoyi and Hedong armies have already defeated Tian Yue; the Huaixi army has taken Xiangyang; Liang Chongyi's corpse was pulled from a well; five thousand were beheaded on the Han; the Henan army will march north any day—the fall of Zhao and Wei is plain to see."

sentences.zh: 公誠去逆蹈順，倡先歸國，可以建不世功。

translations.literal: If you truly abandon rebellion and follow obedience, taking the lead in returning to the state, you can establish merit without parallel in the age.
translations.idiomatic: "If you abandon rebellion and take the lead in returning to the throne, you can win unparalleled merit."

sentences.zh: 」孝忠然之，遣將程華報滔連和，遣易州錄事參軍事董稹入朝。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong agreed, sent the general Cheng Hua to inform Tao of alliance, and sent Yizhou recorder Dong Zhen to enter court.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong agreed, sent General Cheng Hua to ally with Tao, and sent Yizhou recorder Dong Zhen to court.

sentences.zh: 德宗嘉之，擢孝忠檢校工部尚書、成德軍節度使，令與滔並力。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong praised this, promoted Xiaozhong to acting Minister of Works and military commissioner of the Chengde army, and ordered him to join forces with Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Dezong approved, promoted Xiaozhong to acting minister of works and military commissioner of Chengde, and ordered him to join Tao.

sentences.zh: 孝忠子弟在恒州者皆死。

translations.literal: All of Xiaozhong's sons and younger brothers who were in Hengzhou died.
translations.idiomatic: All of Xiaozhong's sons and younger brothers in Hengzhou were killed.

sentences.zh: 孝忠重德滔，為子茂和聘其女，締約益堅。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong deeply esteemed Tao's virtue, betrothed his son Maohe to Tao's daughter, and their pact grew firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong held Tao in high regard, betrothed his son Maohe to Tao's daughter, and their alliance grew stronger.

sentences.zh: 敗惟嶽於束鹿，滔欲乘勝襲恒州，孝忠乃引軍西北，壁義豐。

translations.literal: They defeated Weiyue at Shulu; Tao wished to follow up the victory and strike Hengzhou; Xiaozhong then led his army northwest and fortified at Yifeng.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Weiyue at Shulu, Tao wanted to press on to Hengzhou; Xiaozhong instead withdrew northwest and fortified at Yifeng.

sentences.zh: 滔疑之，孝忠將佐諫曰：「尚書推赤心於朱司徒，可謂至矣。

translations.literal: Tao grew suspicious; Xiaozhong's officers remonstrated: "The Minister has offered his sincere heart to Minister Zhu—this can be called utmost."
translations.idiomatic: Tao grew suspicious. Xiaozhong's officers urged him: "You have shown Minister Zhu every loyalty—nothing more could be asked."

sentences.zh: 今逆賊已潰，元功不終，後且悔之。

translations.literal: Now the rebel bandits are already routed; if the great achievement is not brought to completion, you will regret it afterward.
translations.idiomatic: "The rebels are already broken; if you do not finish the victory, you will regret it."

sentences.zh: 」孝忠曰：「本求破賊，賊已破矣，而恒州多宿將，迫之則死鬥，緩之則改圖。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong said: "Our aim was to break the bandits; the bandits are already broken. Hengzhou has many veteran generals—press them and they will fight to the death; give them respite and they will change their plans."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong said, "Our aim was to defeat the rebels, and they are defeated. Hengzhou has many veteran commanders—press them and they will fight to the death; give them time and they will change sides."

sentences.zh: 且滔言大而識淺，可以慮始，難與守成。

translations.literal: Moreover Tao's words are grand but his understanding shallow—he can be used to plan the beginning but is hard to rely on for holding what is achieved.
translations.idiomatic: "Besides, Tao talks big but sees little—fine for starting a campaign, unreliable for finishing one."

sentences.zh: 故吾堅壁於此，以待賊之滅耳。

translations.literal: Therefore I hold fast in walls here, simply to wait until the bandits perish of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: "So I hold my walls here and wait for the rebels to destroy themselves."

sentences.zh: 」滔亦止屯束鹿。

translations.literal: Tao also halted and encamped at Shulu.
translations.idiomatic: Tao also halted at Shulu.

sentences.zh: 月餘，王武俊果斬惟嶽以獻。

translations.literal: After more than a month, Wang Wujun indeed beheaded Weiyue and presented the head.
translations.idiomatic: A month later Wang Wujun beheaded Weiyue and presented his head.

sentences.zh: 已而定州刺史楊政義以州降孝忠，遂有易、定。

translations.literal: Thereafter Dingzhou prefect Yang Zhengyi surrendered his prefecture to Xiaozhong, and he thus held Yi and Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Dingzhou prefect Yang Zhengyi surrendered to Xiaozhong, giving him Yi and Ding.

sentences.zh: 時三分成德地，詔定州置軍，名義武，以孝忠為節度、易定滄等州觀察使。

translations.literal: At the time the Chengde territory was divided in three; an edict established an army at Dingzhou named Yiwu, and Xiaozhong was made its commissioner and observation commissioner of Yi, Ding, Cang, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Chengde was then divided three ways; the court created an army at Dingzhou called Yiwu and made Xiaozhong its commissioner and observation commissioner of Yi, Ding, Cang, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 後滔與武俊叛，復遣蔡雄說之，答曰：「吾既為唐臣，而天性樸強，業已效忠，不復助惡矣。

translations.literal: Later when Tao and Wujun rebelled, he again sent Cai Xiong to persuade him; Xiaozhong replied: "I am already a subject of Tang, and by nature I am plain and firm; having already shown loyalty, I will not again aid evil."
translations.idiomatic: When Tao and Wujun later rebelled, Tao again sent Cai Xiong. Xiaozhong replied, "I am already a Tang subject, plain and stubborn by nature; having pledged loyalty once, I will not aid wickedness again."

sentences.zh: 吾與武俊少相狎，然其心喜反覆，不可信。

translations.literal: Wujun and I were familiar in youth, yet his heart delights in reversal and cannot be trusted.
translations.idiomatic: "Wujun and I were close in youth, but he loves treachery and cannot be trusted."

sentences.zh: 幸謝司徒，誌鄙言。

translations.literal: May you thank the Minister on my behalf and record these humble words.
translations.idiomatic: "Please thank the Minister for me and remember these words."

sentences.zh: 」滔復啖以金帛，皆不受。

translations.literal: Tao again tempted him with gold and silks; he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: Tao again offered gold and silks; Xiaozhong refused them all.

sentences.zh: 易、定介二鎮間，乃浚溝壘，脩器械，感厲將士，乘城固守。

translations.literal: Yi and Ding lay between two garrisons; he therefore deepened moats and ramparts, repaired weapons, inspired and encouraged officers and soldiers, and mounted the walls to hold fast.
translations.idiomatic: Yi and Ding lay between two hostile zones, so he deepened ditches and walls, repaired arms, rallied his troops, and held the cities.

sentences.zh: 滔悉兵攻之，帝詔李晟、竇文場率師援孝忠，滔解去，遂全其軍。

translations.literal: Tao committed all his troops to attack; the emperor ordered Li Sheng and Dou Wenchang to lead armies to aid Xiaozhong; Tao lifted the siege and withdrew, and thus his army was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: Tao attacked with his full force; the emperor sent Li Sheng and Dou Wenchang to relieve Xiaozhong; Tao withdrew, and Xiaozhong's army was saved.

sentences.zh: 孝忠因與晟結婚。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong therefore formed a marriage alliance with Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong then sealed the alliance with a marriage to Li Sheng's family.

sentences.zh: 天子出奉天，孝忠遣將楊榮國以銳卒六百佐晟赴難，收京師。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven went out to Fengtian, Xiaozhong sent the general Yang Rongguo with six hundred elite troops to assist Sheng in the crisis and recover the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fled to Fengtian, Xiaozhong sent General Yang Rongguo with six hundred elite troops to aid Li Sheng and recover the capital.

sentences.zh: 興元初，詔同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Xingyuan era, he was appointed by edict as co-associate of the Secretariat and Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Xingyuan era he was appointed co-chancellor by edict.

sentences.zh: 貞元二年，河北蝗，民餓死如積，孝忠與其下同粗淡，日膳裁豆䜺而已，人服其儉，推為賢將。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenyuan, locusts struck Hebei and the people starved to death in heaps; Xiaozhong ate coarse fare with his subordinates, his daily meals limited to beans and bran alone; people admired his frugality and acclaimed him a worthy general.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenyuan, locusts ravaged Hebei and the dead lay in heaps. Xiaozhong shared coarse fare with his men, eating nothing but beans and bran each day; people admired his austerity and hailed him as a worthy commander.

sentences.zh: 明年，檢校司空。

translations.literal: The next year he was made acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed acting minister of works.

sentences.zh: 詔其子茂宗尚義章公主，孝忠遣妻入朝，執親迎禮，賞賚甚厚。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his son Maozong to marry Princess Yizhang; Xiaozhong sent his wife to court to perform the bridegroom's welcoming rites, and rewards were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered his son Maozong to marry Princess Yizhang; Xiaozhong sent his wife to court for the welcoming ceremony and received lavish rewards.

sentences.zh: 五年，為將佐所惑，以兵襲尉州，入之，奉詔還鎮。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, misled by his officers, he led troops to raid Weizhou, entered it, and by edict returned to his garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year his officers misled him into raiding Weizhou; after taking it he returned to his post by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 有司劾擅興，削司空。

translations.literal: The authorities impeached him for unauthorized military action and stripped him of the title Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Officials impeached him for unauthorized military action and stripped him of his title as minister of works.

sentences.zh: 六年，還其官。

translations.literal: In the sixth year his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year his title was restored.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十二，追封上谷郡王，贈太師，謚曰貞武。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-two; posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Shanggu commandery, given the posthumous title Grand Preceptor, with the temple name Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-two and was posthumously made Prince of Shanggu, grand preceptor, with the posthumous name Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 子茂昭、茂宗、茂和。

translations.literal: His sons were Maozhao, Maozong, and Maohe.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Maozhao, Maozong, and Maohe.

sentences.zh: 孝忠子 茂宗茂宗，擢累光祿少卿、左衛將軍。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong's son Maozong: Maozong rose through offices to Vice Chamberlain of Imperial Entertainments and general of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong's son Maozong rose to vice chamberlain of imperial entertainments and general of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 元和中，歷閑廄使。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhe era he served as commissioner of the spare stables.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanhe era he served as commissioner of the spare stables.

sentences.zh: 初，至德時，西戎陷隴右，故隴右監及七廄皆廢，而閑廄私其地入，寶應初，始以其地給貧民。

translations.literal: At first, in the Zhide era, the western barbarians took Longyou; the former Longyou commissioner and the seven stud farms were all abolished, while the spare stables privately absorbed their lands; at the beginning of Baoying, those lands were first given to poor households.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhide era the western tribes seized Longyou; the Longyou commissioner and seven stud farms were abolished, and the spare stables quietly took their lands. Only at the start of Baoying were those lands given to poor families.

sentences.zh: 茂宗恃恩，奏悉收其賦，又奏取麟遊岐陽牧地三百餘頃，民訴諸朝，詔監察御史孫革按行，還奏不可。

translations.literal: Maozong relied on favor, memorialized to collect all their taxes, and again memorialized to take more than three hundred qing of pasture at Linyou and Qiyang; the people appealed to court; an edict ordered investigating censor Sun Ge to inspect on site; he returned and memorialized that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Maozong, relying on imperial favor, petitioned to collect all their taxes and seize more than three hundred qing of pasture at Linyou and Qiyang. The people appealed to court; Censor Sun Ge was sent to investigate and reported that this could not be allowed.

sentences.zh: 茂宗負左右助，誣革所奏不實，復遣侍御史範傳式覆實，乃悉奪其田。

translations.literal: Maozong, relying on help from the emperor's intimates, falsely charged that Ge's memorial was untrue, and again sent attendant censor Fan Chuanshi to verify; the lands were then all seized.
translations.idiomatic: Maozong, backed by court favorites, claimed Sun Ge's report was false and sent Attendant Censor Fan Chuanshi to reinvestigate; the lands were then seized in full.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，岐人列訴，下御史，盡以其地還民。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Changqing, the people of Qi filed a collective appeal; the case went to the censorate, and all the land was returned to the people.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Changqing the people of Qi filed a collective appeal; the censorate ordered all the land returned to them.

sentences.zh: 寶歷初，遷兗海節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoli he was transferred as military commissioner of Yanhai.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Baoli he was made military commissioner of Yanhai.

sentences.zh: 終左龍武統軍。

translations.literal: He ended as commander of the Left Dragon Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as commander of the Left Dragon Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 孝忠子 茂和茂和，歷左武衛將軍。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong's son Maohe: Maohe served as general of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong's son Maohe served as general of the Left Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 裴度討蔡，奏為都押衙。

translations.literal: When Pei Du campaigned against Cai, he memorialized to make Maohe chief military adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When Pei Du campaigned against Cai, he recommended Maohe as chief military adjutant.

sentences.zh: 茂和數以膽勇求自試，謂度無功，辭不行。

translations.literal: Maohe repeatedly asked to prove his courage in battle; saying Du had no merit, he declined to go.
translations.idiomatic: Maohe repeatedly asked to prove himself in battle; claiming Pei Du had no merit, he refused to go.

sentences.zh: 度請斬之以令軍，憲宗曰：「予以其家忠且孝，為卿遠斥。

translations.literal: Du requested execution to discipline the army; Emperor Xianzong said: "For the sake of his family's loyalty and filial piety, I will banish him far away for you."
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du asked to execute him to discipline the army. Emperor Xianzong said, "For his family's loyalty and filial piety, I will banish him far from you instead."

sentences.zh: 」後終諸衛將軍。

translations.literal: Later he ended as a general of the guards.
translations.idiomatic: He later ended as a guard general.

sentences.zh: 孝忠子 茂昭茂昭本名升雲，德宗時賜今名，字豐明。

translations.literal: Xiaozhong's son Maozhao: Maozhao was originally named Shengyun; in Dezong's time he was granted his present name, styled Fengming.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozhong's son Maozhao was originally named Shengyun; Emperor Dezong granted him his present name, courtesy name Fengming.

sentences.zh: 少沈毅，頗通書傳。

translations.literal: In youth he was steady and resolute and was fairly versed in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was steady and resolute and well read in the classics.

sentences.zh: 孝忠時，累擢檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: During Xiaozhong's lifetime he was repeatedly promoted to acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: While his father lived he rose to acting minister of works.

sentences.zh: 孝忠卒，帝拜邕王諒為義武軍節度大使，以茂昭為留後，封延德郡王。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhong died, the emperor appointed Prince of Yong Liang as grand commissioner of the Yiwu army and made Maozhao acting commissioner, enfeoffing him as Prince of Yande commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiaozhong's death the emperor appointed Prince of Yong Liang grand commissioner of the Yiwu army and made Maozhao acting commissioner, enfeoffing him as Prince of Yande.

sentences.zh: 後二年，為節度使。

translations.literal: Two years later he became military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he became military commissioner in full.

sentences.zh: 弟昇璘薄王武俊為人，座上嫚罵，武俊怒，襲義豐、安喜、無極，掠萬餘人，茂昭嬰城，遣人厚謝，乃止。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shenglin despised Wang Wujun's character and reviled him at table; Wujun was enraged, attacked Yifeng, Anxi, and Wuji, carried off more than ten thousand people; Maozhao held the city, sent someone with lavish apologies, and Wujun then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Shenglin despised Wang Wujun and insulted him at a banquet. Wujun attacked Yifeng, Anxi, and Wuji and carried off more than ten thousand people. Maozhao held his cities and sent abject apologies until Wujun withdrew.

sentences.zh: 久之，入朝，為帝從容言河朔事，帝竦聽，曰：「恨見卿晚！

translations.literal: After a long time he entered court and spoke at ease on Hebei affairs; the emperor listened alertly and said: "I regret meeting you so late!"
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he came to court and spoke frankly about Hebei; the emperor listened intently and said, "I regret not meeting you sooner!"

sentences.zh: 」召宴麟德殿，賜良馬、甲第、器幣優具，詔其子克禮尚晉康郡主。

translations.literal: He was summoned to a banquet in Linde Hall, given fine horses, a mansion, and lavish vessels and goods; an edict ordered his son Keli to marry the Princess of Jinkang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was feasted in Linde Hall and given fine horses, a mansion, and lavish gifts; the court ordered his son Keli to marry the Princess of Jinkang.

sentences.zh: 帝方倚之經置北方，會崩，故茂昭每入臨，輒哀不自勝。

translations.literal: The emperor had just been relying on him to manage the north when he suddenly died; therefore whenever Maozhao attended the lying-in-state he was overcome with grief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had been relying on him to manage the north when he died; whenever Maozhao attended the lying-in-state he was overcome with grief.

sentences.zh: 順宗立，進同中書門下平章事，復遣之鎮，賜女樂二人，固辭，車至第門，茂昭引詔使辭曰：「天子女樂，非臣下所宜見。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shunzong ascended, Maozhao was advanced to co-associate of the Secretariat and Chancellery, again sent back to his garrison, and granted two female musicians; he firmly declined; when the carriage reached his gate, Maozhao led the edict-bearer to decline, saying: "The Son of Heaven's female musicians are not what subjects should see."
translations.idiomatic: When Shunzong ascended, Maozhao was made co-chancellor and sent back to his post with a gift of two female musicians. He refused firmly; when the carriage reached his gate he told the envoy, "The emperor's female musicians are not for a subject to receive."

sentences.zh: 昔汾陽、鹹寧、西平、北平皆有大功，故當是賜。

translations.literal: In the past Fenyang, Xianning, Xiping, and Beiping all had great merit, and therefore deserved such gifts.
translations.idiomatic: "Fenyang, Xianning, Xiping, and Beiping all earned such gifts through great merit."

sentences.zh: 今下臣述職以朝，奈何濫賞？

translations.literal: Now your humble servant comes to court only to report on duty—how can rewards be lavished so?
translations.idiomatic: "I come only to report on duty—how can such a reward be lavished on me?"

sentences.zh: 後日有立功之臣，陛下何以加之？

translations.literal: If in future there are ministers who achieve merit, how will Your Majesty reward them?
translations.idiomatic: "When ministers who truly earn merit appear, what will Your Majesty have left to give them?"

sentences.zh: 」復賜安仁裏第，亦讓不受。

translations.literal: A mansion in Anren Lane was again granted; he also declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was also offered a mansion in Anren Lane and declined that as well.

sentences.zh: 憲宗元和二年，請朝，五奏乃聽。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanhe under Xianzong he requested audience; only after five memorials was he permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yuanhe under Xianzong he petitioned to come to court; permission came only after five requests.

sentences.zh: 願留，不許，加兼太子太保。

translations.literal: He wished to remain but was not allowed; he was additionally made Grand Protector of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to stay at court but was refused and made grand protector of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 既還，王承宗叛，詔河東、河中、振武、義武合軍為恒州北道招討，茂昭治廩廄，列亭候，平易道路，以待西軍。

translations.literal: After he returned, Wang Chengzong rebelled; an edict ordered Hedong, Hezhong, Zhenwu, and Yiwu to unite armies as northern-route campaign commissioners against Hengzhou; Maozhao repaired granaries and stables, set up courier posts, and leveled roads to await the western armies.
translations.idiomatic: After his return Wang Chengzong rebelled. The court ordered Hedong, Hezhong, Zhenwu, and Yiwu to unite for a northern campaign; Maozhao repaired granaries and stables, set up courier posts, and cleared roads for the western armies.

sentences.zh: 承宗以騎二萬逾木刀溝與王師薄戰，茂昭躬擐甲為前鋒，令其子克讓、從子克儉與諸軍分左右翼繞賊，大敗之，承宗幾危。

translations.literal: Chengzong with twenty thousand cavalry crossed Mudao Ravine and fought a close battle with the imperial army; Maozhao personally donned armor as vanguard, ordered his son Kerang and nephew Kejian with the various armies to flank the bandits left and right, routed them utterly, and Chengzong was nearly destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong crossed Mudao Ravine with twenty thousand cavalry and fought the imperial army at close quarters. Maozhao led the vanguard in armor, sent his son Kerang and nephew Kejian to flank the enemy, and routed them; Chengzong was nearly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 會有詔班師，加檢校太尉，兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: Just then an edict ordered withdrawal; he was promoted to acting Grand Marshal and concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered withdrawal; he was made acting grand marshal and grand tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 乃請舉宗還朝，表數上，帝乃許。

translations.literal: He then requested to bring his whole clan back to court; after several memorials the emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: He then petitioned to bring his entire clan to court; after several memorials the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 北鎮遣客間說，皆不納。

translations.literal: The northern garrisons sent agents to persuade him in secret; he accepted none of them.
translations.idiomatic: Northern garrisons sent secret envoys to dissuade him; he refused them all.

sentences.zh: 詔左庶子任迪簡為行軍司馬，乘驛往代。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Left Household Companion Ren Dijian as campaign marshal and sent him by post-horse to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed Left Household Companion Ren Dijian campaign marshal and sent him by relay to replace Maozhao.

sentences.zh: 茂昭奉兩州符節、管鑰、圖籍歸之。

translations.literal: Maozhao handed over the tallies, keys, and registers of the two prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhao surrendered the seals, keys, and registers of both prefectures.

sentences.zh: 先敕妻子上道，戒曰：「吾使而曹出易，庶後世不為汙俗所染。

translations.literal: He first ordered wife and children onto the road, admonishing: "I make you leave Yi so that later generations may not be stained by corrupt custom."
translations.idiomatic: He sent his wife and children ahead with the warning, "I am taking you out of Yi so our descendants will not be corrupted by frontier ways."

sentences.zh: 」未半道，迎拜兼中書令，充河中晉絳慈隰節度使。

translations.literal: Before he was halfway, he was met and appointed concurrent Director of the Secretariat and military commissioner of Hezhong, Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Before he was halfway to the capital he was met and appointed director of the Secretariat and military commissioner of Hezhong, Jin, Jiang, Ci, and Xi.

sentences.zh: 至京師，雙日開延英，對五刻罷。

translations.literal: On reaching the capital, on a paired day Yingying Hall was opened; audience lasted five quarter-hours before dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the capital he was received in Yingying Hall for an audience of five quarter-hours.

sentences.zh: 又表遷墳墓於京兆，許之。

translations.literal: He again memorialized to move his ancestral graves to Jingzhao; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to move his family's graves to the capital region, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 明年，疽發於首卒，年五十，冊贈太師，謚曰獻武。

translations.literal: The next year an abscess broke out on his head and he died at fifty; by patent he was posthumously made Grand Preceptor, with the temple name Xianwu.
translations.idiomatic: The next year an abscess on his head killed him at fifty; he was posthumously made grand preceptor with the name Xianwu.

sentences.zh: 帝思其忠，擢諸子皆要職，歲給絹二千匹。

translations.literal: The emperor recalled his loyalty, promoted all his sons to important posts, and granted two thousand bolts of silk yearly.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering his loyalty, the emperor gave all his sons important posts and two thousand bolts of silk each year.

sentences.zh: 茂昭少子 克勤少子克勤，開成中歷左武衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Maozhao's youngest son Keqin: the youngest son Keqin, in the Kaicheng era, served as great general of the Left Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhao's youngest son Keqin served as great general of the Left Martial Guard in the Kaicheng era.

sentences.zh: 有詔賜一子五品官，克勤以息幼，推與其甥，吏部員外郎裴夷直劾曰：「克勤骫有司法，引庇它族，開後日賣爵之端，不可許。

translations.literal: An edict granted one son a fifth-rank office; Keqin, because his son was young, yielded it to his nephew; Vice Minister of Personnel Pei Yizhi impeached, saying: "Keqin has twisted the law, extending protection to another clan and opening the way for future sale of offices—this cannot be permitted."
translations.idiomatic: An edict granted a fifth-rank office to one of his sons. Keqin, whose own son was young, gave it to his nephew. Vice Minister Pei Yizhi impeached him: "Keqin has perverted the law, favored another clan, and opened the door to selling offices—this must not stand."

sentences.zh: 」詔聽，遂著於令。

translations.literal: The edict was heeded, and the rule was then written into statute.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed, and the rule was written into law.

sentences.zh: 附 裴夷直夷直字禮卿，亦幸亮，第進士，歷右拾遺，累進中書舍人。

translations.literal: Appended: Pei Yizhi—Yizhi, styled Liqing, also Xingliang, passed the jinshi examination, served as Right Reminder, and rose to Secretariat Draftsman.
translations.idiomatic: Appended biography: Pei Yizhi, courtesy name Liqing, also known as Xingliang, passed the jinshi examination, served as right reminder, and rose to secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，夷直視冊牒，不肯署，乃出為杭州刺史，斥州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: When Wuzong ascended, Yizhi viewed the enthronement documents and refused to sign; he was then sent out as prefect of Hangzhou and demoted to revenue adjutant of the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong ascended, Yizhi inspected the enthronement documents and refused to sign. He was exiled as prefect of Hangzhou and demoted to revenue adjutant.

sentences.zh: 宣宗初內徙，復拜江、華等州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xuanzong he was moved inland and again appointed prefect of Jiang, Hua, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuanzong's reign he was recalled inland and again made prefect of Jiang, Hua, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 終散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He ended as Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 茂昭甥 陳楚陳楚者，茂昭甥也，字材卿，定州人。

translations.literal: Maozhao's nephew Chen Chu: Chen Chu was Maozhao's nephew, styled Caiqing, a man of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Maozhao's nephew Chen Chu, courtesy name Caiqing, was from Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 有武幹，事茂昭，歷牙將，常統精卒從征伐。

translations.literal: He had military ability, served Maozhao, rose through posts as garrison commander, and often led elite troops on campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: A capable soldier, he served Maozhao, rose through garrison commands, and often led elite troops in campaigns.

sentences.zh: 茂昭入朝，擢諸衛大將軍，封普寧郡王。

translations.literal: When Maozhao entered court, Chu was promoted to great general of the guards and enfeoffed as Prince of Puning commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Maozhao came to court, Chu was made great general of the guards and enfeoffed as Prince of Puning.

sentences.zh: 元和末，義武節度使渾鎬喪師，定州亂，拜楚為節度使，馳傳赴軍。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanhe, Yiwu military commissioner Hun Hao lost his army; Dingzhou fell into disorder; Chu was appointed military commissioner and rushed by relay to the army.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yuanhe, Yiwu commissioner Hun Hao lost his army and Dingzhou rebelled. Chu was appointed commissioner and rushed there by relay.

sentences.zh: 及郊，無迎者，左右勸無入，楚曰：「定軍不來迎以試我。

translations.literal: On reaching the suburbs there was no one to welcome him; those beside him urged him not to enter; Chu said: "The Ding army did not come to welcome me in order to test me."
translations.idiomatic: At the city outskirts no one came to meet him. His attendants urged him not to enter. Chu said, "The Ding garrison stayed away to test me."

sentences.zh: 今不入，正墮計中。

translations.literal: "If I do not enter now, I shall fall right into their scheme."
translations.idiomatic: "If I do not enter now, I fall into their trap."

sentences.zh: 」乃冒雪行四十里，夜入其州，然軍校部伍，皆楚舊也，由是眾心乃定。

translations.literal: He then traveled forty li through snow, entered the prefecture by night; yet the officers and ranks were all Chu's old subordinates, and thereby the hearts of the masses were settled.
translations.idiomatic: He marched forty li through snow and entered the city by night. The officers and ranks were all his old men, and the army's hearts were steadied.

sentences.zh: 徙河陽三城，入為左羽林統軍，檢校司空。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Three Cities of Heyang, entered court as commander of the Left Feathered Forest Army, and made acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Three Cities of Heyang, then recalled as commander of the Left Feathered Forest Army and acting minister of works.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十一，贈司空。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-one and was posthumously given the title Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-one and was posthumously made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 子君奕，亦至鳳翔節度使。

translations.literal: His son Junyi also rose to military commissioner of Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Junyi also rose to military commissioner of Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: = 康日知 =

translations.literal: = Kang Rizhi =
translations.idiomatic: Kang Rizhi

sentences.zh: 康日知，靈州人。

translations.literal: Kang Rizhi was a man of Lingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Rizhi was from Lingzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖植，當開元時，縛康待賓，平六胡州，玄宗召見，擢左武衛大將軍，封天山縣男。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhi, in the Kaiyuan era, captured Kang Daibin and pacified the Six Hu prefectures; Xuanzong summoned him, promoted him to great general of the Left Martial Guard, and enfeoffed him as Baron of Tianshan county.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhi, in the Kaiyuan era, captured Kang Daibin and pacified the Six Hu prefectures. Xuanzong summoned him, made him great general of the Left Martial Guard, and enfeoffed him as Baron of Tianshan.

sentences.zh: 日知少事李惟嶽，擢累趙州刺史。

translations.literal: In youth Rizhi served Li Weiyue and rose through offices to prefect of Zhaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Rizhi served Li Weiyue and rose to prefect of Zhaozhou.

sentences.zh: 惟嶽叛，日知與別駕李濯及部將百人啐牲血共盟，固州自歸。

translations.literal: When Weiyue rebelled, Rizhi with Vice Prefect Li Zhuo and a hundred subordinate generals spat sacrificial blood and swore a joint oath, holding the prefecture and returning to allegiance on their own.
translations.idiomatic: When Weiyue rebelled, Rizhi joined Vice Prefect Li Zhuo and a hundred officers in a blood oath and held Zhaozhou for the court.

sentences.zh: 惟嶽怒，遣先鋒兵馬使王武俊攻之，日知使客謝武俊曰：「賊孱甚，安足共安危哉？

translations.literal: Weiyue was enraged and sent vanguard commander Wang Wujun to attack; Rizhi sent a guest to address Wujun: "The bandits are very weak—why share fortune and disaster with them?"
translations.idiomatic: Weiyue sent vanguard commander Wang Wujun to attack. Rizhi sent an envoy to Wujun: "The rebels are feeble—why share their fate?"

sentences.zh: 吾城固士和，雖引歲未可下，且賊所恃者田悅耳，悅兵血蔑邢，壕可浮，不能殘半堞，況吾城之完乎？

translations.literal: "Our walls are strong and the soldiers united; though you camp a full year you cannot take them. Moreover the bandits rely only on Tian Yue—Yue's army bloodied Xingzhou, the moats could be floated, yet they could not destroy half a parapet; how much less our intact city?"
translations.idiomatic: "Our walls are strong and our men united; you could camp a year and not take us. The rebels rely only on Tian Yue—his army bloodied Xingzhou, the moats ran with blood, yet he could not breach half a wall. How will he take our intact city?"

sentences.zh: 」又紿為臺檢示曰：「使者賫詔喻中丞，中丞奈何負天子，從小兒跳梁哉？

translations.literal: He also forged an inspection document from the censorate showing: "The envoy bears an edict to instruct the commissioner—commissioner, why betray the Son of Heaven and follow a boy's rebellion?"
translations.idiomatic: He also forged a censorate document: "The envoy brings an edict—Commissioner, why betray the Son of Heaven and follow a boy's rebellion?"

sentences.zh: 」武俊悟，引兵還，斬惟嶽以獻。

translations.literal: Wujun understood, withdrew his troops, beheaded Weiyue, and presented the head.
translations.idiomatic: Wujun understood, withdrew, beheaded Weiyue, and presented his head.

sentences.zh: 德宗美其謀，擢為深趙觀察使，賜實封戶二百。

translations.literal: Dezong praised his stratagem, promoted him to observation commissioner of Shen and Zhao, and granted two hundred households of substantive fief.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong praised his strategy, made him observation commissioner of Shen and Zhao, and granted two hundred taxable households.

sentences.zh: 會武俊拒命，遣將張鐘葵攻趙州，日知破之，上俘京師。

translations.literal: When Wujun defied orders, he sent the general Zhang Zhongkui to attack Zhaozhou; Rizhi defeated him and sent captives to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Wujun defied the court, he sent Zhang Zhongkui against Zhaozhou; Rizhi defeated him and sent captives to the capital.

sentences.zh: 興元元年，以深趙益成德，徙日知奉誠軍節度使，又徙晉絳，加累檢校尚書左僕射，封會稽郡王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xingyuan, Shen and Zhao were added to Chengde; Rizhi was transferred as military commissioner of the Fengcheng army, then again to Jin and Jiang; he was repeatedly promoted to acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and enfeoffed as Prince of Kuaiji commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xingyuan, Shen and Zhao were added to Chengde. Rizhi was transferred to Fengcheng, then to Jin and Jiang, made acting left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, and enfeoffed as Prince of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 貞元初卒，贈太子太師。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of Zhenyuan and was posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in Zhenyuan and was posthumously made grand tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 日知子 誌睦子誌睦，字得眾。

translations.literal: Rizhi's son Zhimu: Zhimu, styled Dezhong.
translations.idiomatic: Rizhi's son Zhimu, courtesy name Dezhong.

sentences.zh: 資趫偉，工馳射。

translations.literal: By nature he was swift and imposing and skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was swift and imposing by nature and skilled in mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 隸右神策軍，遷累大將軍。

translations.literal: He served in the Right Divine Strategy Army and rose to great general.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Right Divine Strategy Army and rose to great general.

sentences.zh: 討張韶，以多兼御史大夫，進平盧軍節度使。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Zhang Shao, for many achievements he was additionally made Censor-in-Chief and advanced to military commissioner of the Pinglu army.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning against Zhang Shao, he was made censor-in-chief for his achievements and promoted to military commissioner of Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 李同捷反，放兵略千乘，誌睦挫其銳，不得逞，遂下蒲臺，盡奪其械。

translations.literal: When Li Tongjie rebelled and sent troops to raid Qiancheng, Zhimu blunted their edge so they could not prevail, then descended on Putai and seized all their arms.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Tongjie rebelled and raided Qiancheng, Zhimu broke his momentum, then took Putai and seized all his weapons.

sentences.zh: 加檢校尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He was additionally made acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 徙涇原，封會稽郡公。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Jingyuan and enfeoffed as Duke of Kuaiji commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Jingyuan and enfeoffed as Duke of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十七，贈司空。

translations.literal: He died at fifty-seven and was posthumously given the title Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-seven and was posthumously made minister of works.

sentences.zh: 誌睦子 承訓子承訓，字敬辭。

translations.literal: Zhimu's son Chengxun: Chengxun, styled Jingci.
translations.idiomatic: Zhimu's son Chengxun, courtesy name Jingci.

sentences.zh: 推門功進累左神武軍將軍。

translations.literal: For merit in storming the gate he rose through offices to general of the Left Divine Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in storming a gate he rose to general of the Left Divine Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 宣宗擢為天德軍防禦使，軍中馬乏，虜來戰，數負，承訓罷冗費，市馬益軍，軍乃奮張。

translations.literal: Xuanzong promoted him to defense commissioner of the Tiande army; horses in the army were scarce, barbarians came to fight and they were often defeated; Chengxun abolished wasteful expenses, bought horses to strengthen the army, and the army then fought with spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong made him defense commissioner of Tiande. Horses were scarce and the army kept losing to barbarian raids. Chengxun cut waste, bought horses, and the army fought with renewed spirit.

sentences.zh: 始，党項破射雕軍洛源鎮，悉俘其人，聞承訓威政，皆還俘不敢謷。

translations.literal: At first the Tangut broke the Shendiao army at Luoyuan garrison and took all captive; hearing of Chengxun's stern rule, they all returned the captives and did not dare make noise.
translations.idiomatic: When Tangut forces destroyed the Shendiao garrison at Luoyuan and took captives, they returned them all on hearing of Chengxun's stern rule and dared make no further trouble.

sentences.zh: 詔檢校工部尚書，封會稽縣男，擢義武節度。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him acting Minister of Works, enfeoffed him as Baron of Kuaiji county, and promoted him to Yiwu military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was made acting minister of works, enfeoffed as Baron of Kuaiji, and promoted to military commissioner of Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 會南詔破安南，詔徙嶺西南道，城邕州，合容管經略使隸之，遂統諸軍行營兵馬。

translations.literal: When Nanzhao destroyed Annan, an edict transferred him to Lingnan West Circuit, walled Yongzhou, combined Rongguan and other frontier commissioners under him, and he then commanded all campaign armies and horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Nanzhao destroyed Annan, he was transferred to Lingnan West, ordered to fortify Yongzhou and take command of Rongguan and all campaign forces.

sentences.zh: 南詔深入，承訓分兵六道出以掩蠻，戰不利，士死十八，唯天平卒二千還屯，闔軍震。

translations.literal: Nanzhao advanced deep; Chengxun divided his troops into six routes to ambush the barbarians; the battle went badly, eighty percent of the soldiers died, only two thousand Ping troops returned to camp, and the whole army was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Nanzhao advanced deep inland. Chengxun sent six columns to ambush them, but the battle went badly—eighty percent of his men died and only two thousand Ping troops returned. The whole army was shaken.

sentences.zh: 於是節度副使李行素完城不出，南詔圍之四日，或請夜出兵襲蠻，承訓意索，不聽。

translations.literal: Thereupon deputy commissioner Li Xingsu completed the walls and did not go out; Nanzhao besieged for four days; some asked to sally by night against the barbarians; Chengxun was irresolute and would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commissioner Li Xingsu held the walled city. Nanzhao besieged it for four days. Some urged a night attack; Chengxun was irresolute and refused.

sentences.zh: 天平裨將陰募勇兒三百，夜縋燒蠻屯，斬首五百，南詔恐，明日解而去。

translations.literal: A Ping deputy general secretly recruited three hundred brave men, lowered themselves by rope at night to burn the barbarian camp, beheaded five hundred; Nanzhao was afraid and lifted the siege the next day.
translations.idiomatic: A Ping deputy secretly recruited three hundred men, slipped out at night, burned the barbarian camp, and took five hundred heads. Nanzhao withdrew the next day in fear.

sentences.zh: 承訓謬言大破賊，告於朝，群臣皆賀，加檢校尚書右僕射，籍子弟姻昵冒賞，而士不及，怨言嚾流。

translations.literal: Chengxun falsely claimed a great defeat of the bandits and reported to court; all the ministers congratulated him; he was promoted to acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; he registered sons, brothers, in-laws, and intimates for rewards they did not deserve, while soldiers received nothing—complaints and angry shouts spread.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun falsely reported a great victory. The court congratulated him and made him acting right vice director. He registered kin and favorites for rewards while soldiers got nothing; angry complaints spread through the army.

sentences.zh: 嶺南東道節度使韋宙白狀宰相，承訓慚，移疾，授右武衛大將軍，分司東都。

translations.literal: Lingnan East Circuit military commissioner Wei Zhou reported the facts to the chief minister; Chengxun was ashamed, pleaded illness, and was appointed great general of the Right Martial Guard with duties at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Lingnan East commissioner Wei Zhou reported the truth to the chief minister. Ashamed, Chengxun pleaded illness and was given a sinecure as great general of the Right Martial Guard in Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，南詔復盜邊。

translations.literal: In the Xiantong era Nanzhao again raided the borders.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiantong era Nanzhao again raided the frontier.

sentences.zh: 武寧兵七百戍桂州，六歲不得代，列校許佶、趙可立因眾怒殺都將，詣監軍使丐糧鎧北還，不許，即擅斧庫，劫戰械，推糧料判官龐勛為長，勒眾上道。

translations.literal: Seven hundred Wuning soldiers garrisoned at Guizhou; for six years they received no relief. The rank officers Xu Ji and Zhao Keli, taking advantage of the troops' anger, killed the chief commander, went to the army supervisor to beg for grain and armor to return north, were refused, then on their own authority broke open the armory, seized weapons of war, made the provisions officer Pang Xun their leader, and drove the men onto the road.
translations.idiomatic: Seven hundred Wuning troops had garrisoned Guizhou for six years without rotation. Rank officers Xu Ji and Zhao Keli, riding the men's fury, killed the chief commander and appealed to the army supervisor for grain and armor to march home northward. When he refused, they broke into the armory on their own, seized weapons, made provisions officer Pang Xun their chief, and marched the force away.

sentences.zh: 懿宗遣中人張敬思部送，詔本道觀察使崔彥曾慰安之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yizong sent the eunuch Zhang Jingsi to escort them, and ordered the circuit observer of their command, Cui Yanzeng, to reassure and comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yizong sent the eunuch Zhang Jingsi to escort the troops and ordered their circuit observer, Cui Yanzeng, to reassure them.

sentences.zh: 次潭州，監軍詭奪其兵，勛畏必誅，篡舟循江下，益裒兵，招亡命，收銀刀亡卒艚匿之。

translations.literal: When they reached Tanzhou, the army supervisor treacherously seized their weapons. Pang Xun, fearing certain execution, commandeered boats and went down the river, further gathering troops, recruiting fugitives, and taking in Silver Blade deserters hidden in boats.
translations.idiomatic: At Tanzhou the army supervisor treacherously disarmed them. Pang Xun, fearing he would be executed, seized boats and fled downstream, swelling his ranks with fugitives and deserters from the Silver Blade army hidden aboard river craft.

sentences.zh: 及徐城，謀曰：「吾等叩城大呼，眾必應，前日賞緡五十萬可得也。

translations.literal: When they reached Xucheng, they plotted, saying: "If we beat on the city gate and shout loudly, the people will surely respond; we can obtain the five hundred thousand strings of cash offered the other day."
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Xucheng, they plotted: "If we thunder at the gates, the town will rise. We can claim that five hundred thousand strings of reward cash promised earlier."

sentences.zh: 」眾喜。

translations.literal: " The crowd rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: The men cheered.

sentences.zh: 牙健趙武等欲亡，勛斬首送彥曾曰：「此搖亂者。

translations.literal: The garrison guards Zhao Wu and others wished to flee. Pang Xun beheaded them and sent their heads to Yanzeng, saying: "These were agitators."
translations.idiomatic: Garrison guards Zhao Wu and others tried to desert. Pang Xun cut off their heads and sent them to Cui Yanzeng with the message: "These men were stirring trouble."

sentences.zh: 」彥曾不能詰。

translations.literal: " Cui Yanzeng could not interrogate him.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yanzeng could not press the matter.

sentences.zh: 勛怨都押衙尹戡、教練使杜璋、兵馬使徐行儉，又使白彥曾曰：「士負罪，不敢釋甲，請為二屯。

translations.literal: Pang Xun resented the chief adjutant Yin Kan, the training commissioner Du Zhang, and the horse and arms commissioner Xu Xingjian, and also had someone tell Yanzeng: "The men bear guilt and dare not lay aside their armor; please allow two camps."
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun bore a grudge against chief adjutant Yin Kan, training commissioner Du Zhang, and horse commissioner Xu Xingjian. He sent word to Cui Yanzeng: "The men are guilty and dare not disarm. Let us camp in two places."

sentences.zh: 」且白退戡等。

translations.literal: " And asked that Kan and the others be withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: He also demanded that Yin Kan and the others be removed.

sentences.zh: 府屬溫廷皓謂彥曾曰：「勛擅委戍，一可殺。

translations.literal: The staff member Wen Tinghao said to Yanzeng: "Pang Xun on his own abandoned his post — reason one to kill him."
translations.idiomatic: Staff officer Wen Tinghao told Cui Yanzeng: "Pang Xun abandoned his post without orders — one reason to kill him."

sentences.zh: 專戕大將，二可殺。

translations.literal: He arbitrarily killed a senior general — reason two to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: He killed a senior commander on his own authority — a second reason.

sentences.zh: 私置兵，三可殺。

translations.literal: He privately assembled troops — reason three to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: He raised a private army — a third.

sentences.zh: 士不子弟即父兄，振袂而唱，內外必應，銀刀亡命，復在其中，四可殺。

translations.literal: The soldiers are not strangers but sons and brothers; if you raise your sleeve and proclaim, inside and outside will surely respond; Silver Blade fugitives are among them again — reason four to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: These soldiers are locals — sons and brothers — who will rally if you give the signal; fugitives from the Silver Blade force are mixed among them — a fourth reason.

sentences.zh: 請分兩營，脅去三將，五可殺。

translations.literal: He asks to divide into two camps and drive off the three commanders — reason five to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: He wants two camps and the removal of the three officers — a fifth.

sentences.zh: 」彥曾謂然。

translations.literal: " Yanzeng agreed this was so.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yanzeng agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃祃纛黃堂前，選兵三千授都虞候元密。

translations.literal: Then he unfurled the banner before the yellow hall, selected three thousand soldiers, and gave them to the deputy commander Yuan Mi.
translations.idiomatic: He raised the battle standard before the hall, picked three thousand men, and put them under deputy commander Yuan Mi.

sentences.zh: 屯任山，須勛至劫取之，遣邏子贏服覘賊。

translations.literal: They encamped at Renshan, waiting for Xun to arrive to seize him, and sent scouts in tattered clothes to spy on the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Mi camped at Mount Ren to intercept Pang Xun and sent scouts in ragged clothes to watch the rebels.

sentences.zh: 比暮，勛至，捕覘者，知其謀，即蕝偶人，剚虛幟，而詭路襲苻離。

translations.literal: By evening Xun arrived, captured the spies, learned of the plan, then set up straw dummies and planted empty banners, and by a deceptive route attacked Fu Li.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Pang Xun arrived, seized the scouts, learned of the ambush, left straw dummies and empty banners as decoys, and took a detour to strike Fu Li.

sentences.zh: 密久乃寤，回屯城南。

translations.literal: Mi only after a long time understood, and withdrew to encamp south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Mi realized the ruse only belatedly and pulled his camp back south of the city.

sentences.zh: 勛與宿將喬翔戰睢河，翔大敗，攝太守焦璐遁去。

translations.literal: Xun fought the veteran general Qiao Xiang at the Sui River; Xiang was greatly defeated, and the acting prefect Jiao Lu fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun fought veteran general Qiao Xiang at the Sui River. Qiao was routed, and acting prefect Jiao Lu fled.

sentences.zh: 勛入據州，自稱兵馬留後。

translations.literal: Xun entered and seized the prefecture, and styled himself military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun occupied the prefecture and declared himself military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 初，璐決汴水，絕勛北道，水未至，勛度，比密兵攻宿，水大至，涉而傅城，不克攻。

translations.literal: Earlier, Lu had diverted the Bian River to cut off Xun's northern route; the water had not yet arrived when Xun crossed. By the time Mi's troops attacked Su, the water came in full flood; they waded through and reached the walls but could not take the city.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jiao Lu had diverted the Bian River to block Pang Xun's northern route. The flood had not yet risen when Pang crossed, but by the time Yuan Mi's troops assaulted Su, the waters surged. They waded through to the walls yet failed to take the city.

sentences.zh: 勛劫百艘運糧趨泗州，留婦弱持陬。

translations.literal: Xun seized a hundred boats carrying grain and hurried toward Sizhou, leaving women and the weak to hold the corner position.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun seized a hundred grain boats and hurried toward Sizhou, leaving women and noncombatants to hold the rear position.

sentences.zh: 翌日，密覺，追之，士未食。

translations.literal: The next day Mi realized it and pursued them; the soldiers had not yet eaten.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yuan Mi discovered the move and gave chase before his men had eaten.

sentences.zh: 賊伏兵於舟而陣汴上，軍見密皆走。

translations.literal: The rebels hid troops in boats and formed up on the Bian River bank; when the army saw Mi they all fled.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels concealed troops aboard boats and lined up on the Bian River bank. Yuan Mi's soldiers fled at the sight of them.

sentences.zh: 密追躡，伏發，夾攻之，密敗，眾殲。

translations.literal: Mi pursued close on their heels; the ambush sprang, attacked from both sides, Mi was defeated, and his force was annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Mi pressed the pursuit; the ambush erupted and struck from both flanks. He was defeated and his entire force wiped out.

sentences.zh: 遂入徐州，囚彥曾及官屬，殺尹戡等。

translations.literal: Then he entered Xuzhou, imprisoned Yanzeng and the officials, and killed Yin Kan and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun then entered Xuzhou, imprisoned Cui Yanzeng and the officials, and killed Yin Kan and the others.

sentences.zh: 又徇下邳、漣水、宿遷、臨淮、蘄、虹諸縣，皆下。

translations.literal: He also campaigned through Xiapi, Lianshui, Suqian, Linhuai, Qi, and Hong counties; all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He also swept through Xiapi, Lianshui, Suqian, Linhuai, Qi, and Hong counties, and all fell.

sentences.zh: 遣偽將屯柳子，屯豐，屯滕，屯沛，屯蕭，以張其軍，乃露章求節度使。

translations.literal: He sent false generals to garrison Liuzi, Feng, Teng, Pei, and Xiao to inflate his army, then submitted an open memorial requesting the post of military governor.
translations.idiomatic: He posted fake generals at Liuzi, Feng, Teng, Pei, and Xiao to inflate his army, then submitted an open petition demanding the military governorship.

sentences.zh: 有周重者，隱濠、泗間，號有謀，勛迎為上客，問策所出，因教勛：「赦囚徒，據揚州，北收兗、鄆，西舉汴、宋，東掠青、齊，拓境大河，食敖倉，可以持久。

translations.literal: There was a Zhou Zhong who lived in hiding between Hao and Si, reputed for his stratagems. Xun welcomed him as an honored guest, asked where strategy should come from, and he therefore advised Xun: "Pardon prisoners, hold Yangzhou, gather Yan and Yun to the north, raise Bian and Song to the west, plunder Qing and Qi to the east, extend the border to the Great River, feed on the Ao granary — you can endure long."
translations.idiomatic: A man named Zhou Zhong lived in hiding between Hao and Si, reputed for his counsel. Pang Xun welcomed him as an honored guest and asked his strategy. Zhou advised: "Free the prisoners, hold Yangzhou, seize Yan and Yun to the north, take Bian and Song to the west, raid Qing and Qi to the east, expand to the Yellow River, and live off the Ao granary — then you can endure."

sentences.zh: 」勛無雄才，不納。

translations.literal: " Xun lacked heroic talent and did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun lacked grand ambition and ignored the advice.

sentences.zh: 偽將劉行及攻濠州，執刺史盧望回，自稱刺史。

translations.literal: The false general Liu Xingji attacked Haozhou, seized the prefect Lu Wanghui, and styled himself prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Liu Xingji attacked Haozhou, captured prefect Lu Wanghui, and declared himself prefect.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中人康道隱宣慰徐州，勛郊迎，旗鎧矛戟亙三十里，使騎鳴鼙角，聲動山谷。

translations.literal: The emperor sent the eunuch Kang Daoyin to reassure Xuzhou. Xun met him outside the city; banners, armor, spears, and halberds stretched thirty li; he had horsemen sound drums and horns, and the noise shook the valleys.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent the eunuch Kang Daoyin to reassure Xuzhou. Pang Xun met him outside the city with banners, armor, spears, and halberds stretching thirty li, cavalry sounding drums and horns until the noise shook the valleys.

sentences.zh: 置酒球球場，引道隱閱其眾，紿為賊來降六十人，妄戮平民，上首級誇勝。

translations.literal: He set out wine at the ball ground, led Daoyin to review his troops, falsely claimed sixty rebels had come to surrender, wantonly slaughtered civilians, and presented severed heads to boast of victory.
translations.idiomatic: He hosted a feast at the ball field, paraded his troops before Daoyin, falsely claimed sixty rebels had surrendered, killed civilians at random, and presented severed heads to boast of victory.

sentences.zh: 」道隱還，固求節度。

translations.literal: " Daoyin returned, and Xun persistently demanded the military governorship.
