translations.idiomatic: When Daoyin returned, Pang Xun persistently demanded the military governorship.

sentences.zh: 即殘魚臺、金鄉、碭山、單父十餘縣，斬官吏，出金帛募兵，遊民多從之。

translations.literal: He then ravaged Yutai, Jinxiang, Dangshan, Shanfu, and more than ten other counties, beheaded officials, distributed gold and silk to recruit troops, and many vagrants followed him.
translations.idiomatic: He then ravaged Yutai, Jinxiang, Dangshan, Shanfu, and more than ten other counties, executed officials, distributed gold and silk to recruit troops, and many vagrants joined him.

sentences.zh: 帝乃拜承訓檢校尚書右僕射、義成軍節度使、徐泗行營都招討使，以神武大將軍王晏權為武寧軍節度使、北面行營招討使，羽林將軍戴可師為南面行營招討使，率魏博、鄜延、義武、鳳翔、沙陀、吐渾兵二十萬討之。

translations.literal: The emperor then appointed Cheng Xun acting Right Vice Minister of Works, military governor of Yicheng, and supreme campaign commander of the Xu-Si field headquarters; made the Shenwu grand general Wang Yanquan military governor of Wuning and northern campaign commander; made the Imperial Guard general Dai Keshi southern campaign commander; and led two hundred thousand troops from Weibo, Fuyan, Yiwu, Fengxiang, Shatuo, and Tuhun to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then appointed Kang Chengxun acting Right Vice Minister of Works, military governor of Yicheng, and supreme commander of the Xu-Si campaign; made Shenwu grand general Wang Yanquan military governor of Wuning and northern campaign commander; made Imperial Guard general Dai Keshi southern campaign commander; and sent two hundred thousand troops from Weibo, Fuyan, Yiwu, Fengxiang, Shatuo, and Tuhun against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 勛好鬼道，有言漢高祖廟夜閱兵，人馬流汗，勛日往請命。

translations.literal: Xun favored ghostly ways. There were reports that at the Han Gaozu temple troops were reviewed by night and men and horses sweated. Xun went daily to seek mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun dabbled in occult practices. Reports held that the Han Gaozu temple reviewed troops by night, men and horses streaming with sweat. He visited daily to seek a mandate.

sentences.zh: 巫言球場有隱龍，得之可戰勝，勛大役徒鑿地，不能得。

translations.literal: Shamans said there was a hidden dragon at the ball ground; obtaining it would bring victory in battle. Xun conscripted labor on a grand scale to dig the earth but could not obtain it.
translations.idiomatic: Shamans claimed a hidden dragon lay beneath the ball field and that capturing it would ensure victory. Pang Xun mobilized masses of laborers to dig but found nothing.

sentences.zh: 賊將李圓、劉佶攻泗，歐宗、丁從實分徇舒、廬、壽、沂、海諸道。

translations.literal: The rebel generals Li Yuan and Liu Ji attacked Si; Ou Zong and Ding Congshi separately campaigned through the circuits of Shu, Lu, Shou, Yi, and Hai.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel generals Li Yuan and Liu Ji attacked Sizhou while Ou Zong and Ding Congshi separately swept through Shu, Lu, Shou, Yi, and Hai.

sentences.zh: 兵屯海州，度賊至，作機橋，雜以長縆，賊半度，縆絕，半溺死，度者不得戰，殲之。

translations.literal: Troops encamped at Haizhou. Anticipating the rebels' arrival, they built a treacherous bridge mixed with long ropes. When half the rebels had crossed, the ropes broke; half drowned. Those who had crossed could not fight, and all were annihilated.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial troops at Haizhou, anticipating the rebels, built a treacherous bridge rigged with long ropes. When half the enemy was across, the ropes snapped and half drowned. Those who had crossed could not fight, and all were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 賊別取和州，破沐陽、下蔡、烏江、巢諸縣，揚州大恐，民悉度江。

translations.literal: Rebels separately took Hezhou and broke Muyang, Xia'ai, Wujiang, and Chao counties. Yangzhou was greatly terrified, and the people all crossed the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel forces separately took Hezhou and overran Muyang, Xia'ai, Wujiang, and Chao. Yangzhou panicked, and the people fled across the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 淮南節度使令狐移書陳禍福，許助求節度，勛按甲聽命。

translations.literal: The Huai-nan military governor Linghu Tao sent a letter setting forth fortune and disaster, promising to help him seek the military governorship. Xun halted his arms and listened to orders.
translations.idiomatic: Huai-nan military governor Linghu Tao sent a letter weighing the stakes, promising to help secure the military governorship. Pang Xun halted and waited.

sentences.zh: 淮南合宣、潤兵戍都梁山。

translations.literal: Huai-nan combined the troops of Xuan and Run to garrison Duliang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Huai-nan combined Xuan and Run troops to garrison Duliang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 勛夜度淮，曙薄壘，賊將劉行立、王弘立與勛合，敗淮南將李湘，屯淮口，劫盱眙。

translations.literal: Xun crossed the Huai by night; at dawn he pressed the fort. The rebel generals Liu Xingli and Wang Hongli joined with Xun, defeated the Huai-nan general Li Xiang, encamped at Huaikou, and plundered Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun crossed the Huai by night and reached the fort at dawn. Rebel generals Liu Xingli and Wang Hongli joined him, defeated Huai-nan general Li Xiang, camped at Huaikou, and plundered Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 帝又詔將軍宋威與淮南並力。

translations.literal: The emperor also ordered the general Song Wei to join forces with Huai-nan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ordered general Song Wei to cooperate with Huai-nan.

sentences.zh: 承訓屯新興，賊挑戰，時諸道兵未集，承訓帳下才萬人，退壁宋州。

translations.literal: Cheng Xun encamped at Xinxing; the rebels challenged battle. At the time the troops of the various circuits had not yet assembled; Cheng Xun had only ten thousand men under his command and withdrew to fortify Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Chengxun encamped at Xinxing while the rebels taunted him to fight. Allied troops had not yet assembled, and he had only ten thousand men under his command, so he withdrew to fortify Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 勛益驕。

translations.literal: Xun grew all the more arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun grew bolder.

sentences.zh: 光、蔡鉅賊陷滁州，殺刺史高錫望應勛。

translations.literal: Great bandits of Guang and Cai took Chuzhou, killed the prefect Gao Xi, and looked to Xun to respond.
translations.idiomatic: Major bandits from Guang and Cai took Chuzhou, killed prefect Gao Xi, and rallied to Pang Xun.

sentences.zh: 戴可師引兵三萬奪淮口，圍勛都梁山下，降其眾。

translations.literal: Dai Keshi led thirty thousand troops to seize Huaikou, besieged Xun at the foot of Duliang Mountain, and accepted the surrender of his followers.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Keshi led thirty thousand troops to retake Huaikou, besieged Pang Xun at the foot of Duliang Mountain, and accepted the surrender of his followers.

sentences.zh: 可師恃勝不戒，弘立以兵襲之，可師不克陣而潰，士溺淮死，逸者數百人，賊取可師首傳徐州。

translations.literal: Keshi, relying on victory, took no precautions. Hongli attacked him with troops. Keshi could not hold formation and fled; soldiers drowned in the Huai and died; only several hundred escaped. The rebels took Keshi's head and displayed it at Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Keshi, overconfident after victory, was ambushed by Wang Hongli. He failed to hold formation and routed; soldiers drowned in the Huai, and only a few hundred escaped. The rebels took his head and paraded it at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 詔以馬士舉為淮南節度使、南面行營諸軍都統，馳傳入揚州。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Ma Shiju Huai-nan military governor and supreme commander of all southern campaign armies; he entered Yangzhou by express relay.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shiju was appointed Huai-nan military governor and supreme commander of the southern campaign, and rode express post into Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 士舉曰：「城堅士多，賊何能為？

translations.literal: Shiju said: "The walls are strong and the soldiers many — what can the rebels do?"
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shiju said: "The walls are strong and our soldiers are many — what can the rebels do?"

sentences.zh: 」眾稍安。

translations.literal: " The people gradually calmed.
translations.idiomatic: The people gradually calmed.

sentences.zh: 始，帝以晏權故智興子，節度武寧，欲以怖賊。

translations.literal: At first the emperor had made Yanquan — the former Zhixing's son — military governor of Wuning, intending to intimidate the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Initially the emperor had made Wang Yanquan — son of the former Wang Zhixing — military governor of Wuning to intimidate the rebels.

sentences.zh: 及是，返為賊困，不敢戰，乃更以隴州刺史曹翔為兗海節度、北面都統招討使，屯滕、沛，魏博將薛尤屯蕭、豐。

translations.literal: By this time he was instead trapped by the rebels and dared not fight. The emperor then replaced him with the Longzhou prefect Cao Xiang as Yan-Hai military governor and northern supreme campaign commander, encamping at Teng and Pei; the Weibo general Xue You encamped at Xiao and Feng.
translations.idiomatic: By then he was trapped by the rebels and dared not fight. Cao Xiang, prefect of Longzhou, replaced him as Yan-Hai military governor and northern supreme commander, encamping at Teng and Pei, while Weibo general Xue You held Xiao and Feng.

sentences.zh: 賊首孟敬文欲絕勛自立，陰刻鑒為文曰「天口云云，錫爾將軍」，夜瘞之野，耕者得之以獻，眾駭異，乃齋三日授之。

translations.literal: The rebel chief Meng Jingwen wished to break from Xun and establish himself. He secretly carved a mirror with the inscription "Heaven's mouth declares thus: I grant you the title of general," buried it in the wild by night; a farmer obtained it and presented it. The crowd was awed and astonished, and after three days of fasting they invested him.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel chief Meng Jingwen sought to break from Pang Xun and rule alone. He secretly carved a mirror inscribed "Heaven's mouth declares: I grant you the title of general" and buried it by night. A farmer found it and presented it; the crowd was awed, and after three days of fasting they invested him.

sentences.zh: 勛知其謀，使人襲殺之。

translations.literal: Xun learned of the plot and sent men to ambush and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun learned of the plot and sent men to ambush and kill him.

sentences.zh: 於是承訓屯柳子右，夾汴築壘，連屬一舍。

translations.literal: Thereupon Cheng Xun encamped to the right of Liuzi, built ramparts along both banks of the Bian, and connected them for thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Chengxun then encamped east of Liuzi and built ramparts along both banks of the Bian River, linking them for thirty li.

sentences.zh: 勛籍城中兵，止三千，劫民授甲，皆穿窟穴遁去。

translations.literal: Xun registered the troops in the city — only three thousand. When he forced the people to take armor, all tunneled through holes and fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun mustered the city's troops and found only three thousand. When he forced civilians into armor, they all dug tunnels and fled.

sentences.zh: 王弘立度睢，圍新興、鹿塘。

translations.literal: Wang Hongli crossed the Sui and besieged Xinxing and Lutang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Hongli crossed the Sui River and besieged Xinxing and Lutang.

sentences.zh: 承訓縱沙陀騎躪之，弘立走，士赴水死，自鹿塘屬襄城，伏屍五十里，數首二萬，獲器鎧不貲。

translations.literal: Cheng Xun unleashed Shatuo cavalry to trample them. Hongli fled; soldiers rushed into the water and died. From Lutang to Xiangcheng, corpses lay for fifty li; twenty thousand heads were counted; arms and armor captured beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Chengxun unleashed Shatuo cavalry to overrun them. Wang Hongli fled; his soldiers drowned in the water. Corpses lay for fifty li from Lutang to Xiangcheng; twenty thousand heads were counted and arms and armor beyond reckoning were captured.

sentences.zh: 承訓攻柳子，姚周度水戰，又敗，乘風火賊，周提餘卒去，沙陀躡之，及芳亭，死者枕藉，斬劉豐，而周以十騎走宿州，守將斬之。

translations.literal: Cheng Xun attacked Liuzi. Yao Zhou fought on the water and was again defeated. He set fire to the rebels' boats downwind. Zhou led the remaining troops away; Shatuo pursued them. At Fangting the dead piled up; Liu Feng was beheaded. Zhou fled with ten horsemen to Suzhou, and the garrison commander beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Chengxun attacked Liuzi. Yao Zhou fought on the water and lost again; he set fire to rebel boats downwind and withdrew with the survivors. Shatuo cavalry pursued to Fangting, where the dead piled up; Liu Feng was beheaded. Yao Zhou escaped with ten riders to Suzhou, where the garrison commander killed him.

sentences.zh: 勛懼，乃害崔彥曾等，謂其下曰：「上不許我節度，與諸君真反矣。

translations.literal: Xun was afraid, then killed Cui Yanzeng and the others, and said to his followers: "The throne will not grant me the military governorship — with you all I am truly in rebellion now."
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun, afraid, killed Cui Yanzeng and the others and told his followers: "The throne denied me the military governorship — with you I am truly in rebellion now."

sentences.zh: 」大索兵，得三萬。

translations.literal: " He searched broadly for troops and obtained thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned troops broadly and gathered thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 許佶、趙可立勸勛稱「天冊將軍」，勛謁漢高祖廟受命，以其父舉直為大司馬，守徐州。

translations.literal: Xu Ji and Zhao Keli urged Xun to take the title "Heaven-Mandated General." Xun visited the Han Gaozu temple to receive mandate, made his father Ju Zhi grand marshal, and left him to hold Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ji and Zhao Keli urged Pang Xun to take the title "Heaven-Mandated General." He received mandate at the Han Gaozu temple, appointed his father Ju Zhi grand marshal to hold Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「方大事，不可私於父，失上下序。

translations.literal: Someone said: "At a moment of great affairs, you cannot show private favor to your father — it violates the order between superior and inferior."
translations.idiomatic: Someone said: "At this critical moment you cannot favor your father — it violates proper order between ruler and subject."

sentences.zh: 」舉直乃拜於廷，勛坐受之。

translations.literal: " Ju Zhi then bowed in the court, and Xun sat and received it.
translations.idiomatic: Ju Zhi then prostrated himself in court while Pang Xun sat and accepted the bow.

sentences.zh: 引兵救豐，刻木作婦人，衣絳被發，軍過，斫而火之，乃行。

translations.literal: He led troops to relieve Feng, carved wooden figures of women dressed in crimson with hair loose; when the army passed, they chopped and burned them, then marched on.
translations.idiomatic: He led troops to relieve Feng, carving wooden women dressed in crimson with hair loose; as the army passed they chopped and burned them, then marched on.

sentences.zh: 勛夜入城，外不知。

translations.literal: Xun entered the city by night; those outside did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun entered the city by night without outsiders knowing.

sentences.zh: 勛出銳軍擊援屯，魏博軍知勛自將，驚而潰。

translations.literal: Xun sallied with elite troops to strike the relief encampment. The Weibo army, learning that Xun personally commanded, was alarmed and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun sallied with elite troops against the relief camp. The Weibo army, learning Pang Xun commanded in person, panicked and routed.

sentences.zh: 賊以所得送徐州以誇下。

translations.literal: The rebels sent what they had captured to Xuzhou to boast to those below.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent their spoils to Xuzhou to boast to the people.

sentences.zh: 曹翔退保兗州。

translations.literal: Cao Xiang withdrew to defend Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xiang withdrew to defend Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 勛欲乘勝攻承訓，或曰：「今北兵敗，西軍搖，不足虞也。

translations.literal: Xun wished to press the victory and attack Cheng Xun. Someone said: "Now the northern army is defeated and the western army wavers — they are not worth worrying about."
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun wanted to press the victory and attack Kang Chengxun. Someone said: "The northern army is beaten and the western army wavering — no need to worry about them."

sentences.zh: 方蠶月，宜息眾力農，至秋士馬強，決可以取勝。

translations.literal: It is silkworm season; you should rest the troops and put strength into farming. By autumn horses and soldiers will be strong, and victory can surely be taken.
translations.idiomatic: It is silkworm season; rest the men and farm. By autumn horses and soldiers will be strong, and victory is assured.

sentences.zh: 」舉直曰：「時不重得，願將軍無縱敵。

translations.literal: " Ju Zhi said: "Such a moment does not come again; I hope the general will not let the enemy go."
translations.idiomatic: Ju Zhi said: "Such moments do not return — general, do not let the enemy go."

sentences.zh: 」勛曰：「然。

translations.literal: " Xun said: "So it is."
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun said: "Right."

sentences.zh: 」時承訓方攻臨渙，聞勛計，追還兵仗以待。

translations.literal: " At that time Cheng Xun was attacking Linhuan. Hearing Xun's plan, he recalled his troops and arms to wait.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Chengxun was attacking Linhuan; hearing Pang Xun's plan, he recalled his troops and prepared arms to wait.

sentences.zh: 勛軍皆市人，囂而狂，未陣即奔，相蹈藉死者四萬。

translations.literal: Xun's army were all townspeople — noisy and reckless. Before forming ranks they fled; trampling one another, forty thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun's army was townsmen — noisy and reckless. They fled before forming ranks, and forty thousand were trampled to death.

sentences.zh: 勛釋甲服垢襦脫，收夷痕士三千以歸，遣張行實屯第城。

translations.literal: Xun cast off his armor and wore a filthy short coat instead, gathered three thousand wounded soldiers and returned, and sent Zhang Xingshi to garrison Dicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun shed his armor and wore a filthy short coat, gathered three thousand wounded troops, and returned; he sent Zhang Xingshi to garrison Dicheng.

sentences.zh: 馬士舉救泗州，賊解去，進攻賊濠州。

translations.literal: Ma Shiju relieved Sizhou; the rebels lifted the siege and departed. He advanced to attack the rebels' Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Shiju relieved Sizhou; the rebels lifted the siege and he advanced on rebel-held Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 是時，又詔黔中觀察使秦匡謀討賊，下招義、鐘離、定遠。

translations.literal: At this time an edict also ordered the Qianzhong observer Qin Kuangmou to suppress the rebels; he took Zhaoyi, Zhongli, and Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time the Qianzhong observer Qin Kuangmou was ordered to suppress the rebels and took Zhaoyi, Zhongli, and Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 勛遣吳迥屯北津援濠，士舉銳兵度淮，盡碎其營。

translations.literal: Xun sent Wu Jiong to encamp at Beijin to aid Haozhou. Shiju's elite troops crossed the Huai and completely smashed their camps.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun sent Wu Jiong to camp at Beijin to aid Haozhou. Ma Shiju's elite crossed the Huai and smashed all their camps.

sentences.zh: 初，勛之遁，懼眾不軍，妄言有神呼野中曰：「天符下，國兵休。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xun fled, fearing the crowd would not fight, he falsely claimed a spirit cried in the wild: "Heaven's tally descends; the imperial army halts."
translations.idiomatic: When Pang Xun had fled earlier, fearing his troops would not fight, he falsely claimed a god cried in the wild: "Heaven's tally descends — the imperial army halts."

sentences.zh: 」勛使下相語，符未降，故敗北津。

translations.literal: " Xun had men below spread the word to one another. The tally had not descended, and therefore they were defeated at Beijin.
translations.idiomatic: He had men spread the word, but the tally never came — hence the defeat at Beijin.

sentences.zh: 帝恨魏博軍不勝，以宋威為西北面招討使，率兵三萬屯蕭、豐，約勛：「降者當赦之。

translations.literal: The emperor resented that the Weibo army had not won. He made Song Wei northwest campaign commander, leading thirty thousand troops to encamp at Xiao and Feng, and promised Xun: "Those who surrender shall be pardoned."
translations.idiomatic: Resentful that the Weibo army had not won, the emperor made Song Wei northwest campaign commander with thirty thousand troops at Xiao and Feng, promising Pang Xun: "Surrenders will be pardoned."

sentences.zh: 」始，宿鄙人劉洪者，被黃袍，白馬，使人封檄叩觀察府曰：「我當王徐。

translations.literal: " Earlier, a Liu Hong of Suzhou, wearing a yellow robe and riding a white horse, had someone deliver a sealed dispatch knocking at the observer's office, saying: "I shall be king of Xu."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a man named Liu Hong of Suzhou, wearing a yellow robe and riding a white horse, had a sealed letter delivered to the observer's office declaring: "I shall be king of Xu."

sentences.zh: 」崔彥曾斬之，遺黨匿山谷，欲附勛，承訓喻降之。

translations.literal: " Cui Yanzeng beheaded him. The remnant followers hid in mountain valleys, wishing to join Xun; Cheng Xun persuaded them to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yanzeng executed him. Remnant followers hid in the mountains wanting to join Pang Xun; Kang Chengxun persuaded them to surrender.

sentences.zh: 王師破臨渙，斬萬級，收襄城、留武、小睢諸壁。

translations.literal: The imperial army broke Linhuan, beheaded ten thousand ranks, and took the forts of Xiangcheng, Liuwu, and Xiaosui.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army broke Linhuan, took ten thousand heads, and captured the forts at Xiangcheng, Liuwu, and Xiaosui.

sentences.zh: 曹翔下滕，賊將以蘄、沛降，賊李直奔入徐州。

translations.literal: Cao Xiang took Teng. Rebel generals surrendered Qi and Pei; the rebel Li Zhen fled straight into Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xiang took Teng. Rebel generals surrendered Qi and Pei; rebel Li Zhen fled into Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 翔又破豐、徐城、下邳，賊益蹙。

translations.literal: Xiang again broke Feng, Xucheng, and Xiapi; the rebels grew ever more cornered.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Xiang also broke Feng, Xucheng, and Xiapi, and the rebels grew increasingly cornered.

sentences.zh: 勛以張玄稔守宿州，張儒、劉景助之，自稱統軍，列壁相望。

translations.literal: Xun put Zhang Xuancheng to hold Suzhou, with Zhang Ru and Liu Jing assisting him. He styled himself commander-in-chief; camps lined up facing one another.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun put Zhang Xuancheng in charge of Suzhou with Zhang Ru and Liu Jing assisting. He styled himself commander-in-chief, with camps facing one another in lines.

sentences.zh: 承訓拔第城，張行實奔宿州，承訓遂圍宿州。

translations.literal: Cheng Xun took Dicheng. Zhang Xingshi fled to Suzhou, and Cheng Xun then besieged Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Chengxun took Dicheng. Zhang Xingshi fled to Suzhou, and Kang Chengxun besieged Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 行實教勛：「官軍盡銳於此，西鄙虛單，將軍直搗宋、亳，出不意，宿圍自解。

translations.literal: Xingshi advised Xun: "The imperial army has concentrated all its elite here; the western frontier is empty and thin. The general should strike straight at Song and Bo by surprise, and the siege of Suzhou will lift of itself."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xingshi advised Pang Xun: "The imperial army has concentrated all its strength here; the western frontier is empty. Strike Song and Bo unexpectedly and the Suzhou siege will lift itself."

sentences.zh: 」勛喜，引而西，使舉直、許佶守徐。

translations.literal: " Xun was pleased, led his force westward, and left Ju Zhi and Xu Ji to hold Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun was delighted, marched west, and left Ju Zhi and Xu Ji to hold Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 承訓攻敗，十遇皆勝。

translations.literal: Cheng Xun attacked and was victorious; in ten encounters he won every time.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Chengxun attacked and won all ten encounters.

sentences.zh: 遣辯士以威動玄稔。

translations.literal: He sent an eloquent envoy to sway Xuancheng with threats and promises.
translations.idiomatic: He sent an eloquent envoy to sway Zhang Xuancheng with threats and promises.

sentences.zh: 玄稔，賊重將也，以帛書射城外，約誅勛自歸，使張臯獻期。

translations.literal: Xuancheng was a major rebel general. He shot a silk letter outside the city wall, agreeing to kill Xun and surrender himself, and sent Zhang Gao to present the appointed date.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuancheng, a major rebel general, shot a silk letter outside the city agreeing to kill Pang Xun and surrender; he sent Zhang Gao to deliver the appointed date.

sentences.zh: 俄與二將會柳溪，伏士於旁，玄稔馳騎呼曰：「龐勛首已梟僕射寨矣！

translations.literal: Soon he met the two generals at Willow Stream, with hidden soldiers beside them. Xuancheng galloped on horseback and cried: "Pang Xun's head is already displayed at the Vice Minister's camp!"
translations.idiomatic: Soon he met the two generals at Willow Stream with hidden troops nearby. Zhang Xuancheng galloped up shouting: "Pang Xun's head is already displayed at the Vice Minister's camp!"

sentences.zh: 」伏興，斬劉景、張儒。

translations.literal: " The ambush rose; Liu Jing and Zhang Ru were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The ambush rose; Liu Jing and Zhang Ru were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 玄稔率諸將肉袒見承訓，自陳陷賊不早奮，久暴王師，願禽賊贖死。

translations.literal: Xuan Min led the generals, bared their upper bodies, and went to see Cheng Xun, confessing they had fallen among the rebels and had not risen up sooner, that they had long exposed the imperial army to delay, and that they wished to capture the bandits to redeem their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan Min led his generals stripped to the waist before Cheng Xun. They admitted they had served the rebels too long without revolt, had kept the imperial army tied down for months, and begged to capture the rebels and earn their lives back.

sentences.zh: 承訓許之。

translations.literal: Cheng Xun granted the request.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xun agreed.

sentences.zh: 復請詐為潰軍劫符離。

translations.literal: He again requested to feign being a routed army and raid Fuli.
translations.idiomatic: He then asked to pose as a broken army and seize Fuli by surprise.

sentences.zh: 苻離不知，內之，已入，即斬守將，得兵萬人，北攻徐州。

translations.literal: Fuli did not know; they admitted them. Once inside, they immediately beheaded the defending general, obtained ten thousand troops, and attacked Xuzhou from the north.
translations.idiomatic: Fuli's garrison took them in unsuspecting. Once inside they killed the commander, rallied ten thousand men, and marched north on Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 許佶等不敢出。

translations.literal: Xu Ji and the others did not dare come out.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ji and his associates dared not sally forth.

sentences.zh: 玄稔環城，彥曾故吏路審中啟白門內玄稔兵，許佶等啟北門走，玄稔身追之，士大崩，皆赴水死，斬舉直、許佶、李直等，收叛卒親族悉夷之。

translations.literal: Xuan Min encircled the city. Lu Shenzhong, a former officer of Yan Zeng, opened the White Gate to admit Xuan Min's troops; Xu Ji and the others opened the North Gate and fled. Xuan Min personally pursued them; the troops collapsed in panic, all rushed into the water and drowned. Ju Zhi, Xu Ji, Li Zhi, and others were beheaded; the rebel soldiers' kin were all exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan Min besieged the city. Lu Shenzhong, once an officer under Yan Zeng, opened the White Gate to Xuan Min's men while Xu Ji and the rest fled through the North Gate. Xuan Min chased them himself; the rebel host broke and stampeded into the rivers to drown. Ju Zhi, Xu Ji, Li Zhi, and others were executed, and the families of every rebel soldier were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 勛聞徐已拔，氣喪，無顧賴，眾尚二萬，自石山而西，所在焚掠。

translations.literal: When Pang Xun heard that Xu prefecture had been taken, his spirit collapsed; he had nothing to rely on. His force still numbered twenty thousand; from Shishan he went west, burning and plundering wherever he passed.
translations.idiomatic: Learning Xuzhou had fallen, Pang Xun lost heart and saw no way out. With some twenty thousand men left he marched west from Shishan, burning and looting every district in his path.

sentences.zh: 承訓悉兵八萬逐北，沙陀將朱耶赤衷急追至宋州，勛焚南城，為刺史鄭處沖所破，將南趨亳，承訓兵循渙而東，賊走蘄縣，官兵斷橋，不及濟，承訓乃縱擊之，斬首萬級，餘皆溺死。

translations.literal: Cheng Xun mustered eighty thousand troops to pursue north. The Shatuo general Zhuye Chizhong urgently pursued to Song prefecture. Pang Xun burned the south suburbs and was defeated by Prefect Zheng Chongchu. About to flee south toward Bo, Cheng Xun's army followed the Huan River east; the bandits fled to Qi county. Government troops destroyed the bridge so they could not cross; Cheng Xun then unleashed an attack, beheading ten thousand at the head, and the rest all drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xun led eighty thousand men in pursuit. The Shatuo commander Zhuye Chizhong ran them down at Songzhou. Pang Xun torched the south suburbs but was beaten by Prefect Zheng Chongchu and turned toward Bo. Cheng Xun's forces tracked the Huan eastward; the rebels fled to Qi county, found the bridge broken, and could not escape. Cheng Xun drove them into the water—ten thousand heads taken, the rest drowned.

sentences.zh: 閱三日，得勛屍。

translations.literal: After examining for three days, Pang Xun's corpse was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later Pang Xun's body was found.

sentences.zh: 斬其子於京師。

translations.literal: His son was beheaded in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His son was executed in the capital.

sentences.zh: 吳迥守濠州，糧盡食人，驅女孺運薪塞隍，並填之，整旅而行，馬士舉斬以獻。

translations.literal: Wu Yong held Haozhou; when grain was exhausted they ate people, drove women and children to carry firewood and fill the moat, then formed ranks and marched out. Ma Shiju beheaded him and presented the head.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yong held Haozhou until the stores ran out and the garrison began eating the living. He forced women and children to haul firewood and fill the moat, then marched out in column; Ma Shiju cut him down and sent his head to camp.

sentences.zh: 勛之始得徐州，貲儲蕩然，乃四出剽取，男子十五以上皆執兵，舒鉏鉤為兵，號「霍錐」，破十餘州，凡二歲滅。

translations.literal: When Pang Xun first took Xuzhou, stores were utterly depleted; he then raided on all sides. Men fifteen and older all bore arms; plowshares and hooks were bent into weapons, called "Huo Cones." He shattered more than ten prefectures; in all, within two years he was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When Pang Xun first seized Xuzhou his treasury was empty, so he sent raiders in every direction. Every male fifteen or older was armed; hoes and hooks were hammered into spears they called "Huo Cones." He ravaged more than ten prefectures and, within two years, was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 詔擢張玄稔右驍衛大將軍，承訓遷檢校左僕射、同中書門下平章事，徙節河東。

translations.literal: An edict promoted Zhang Xuanmin to General-in-Chief of the Right Brave Guards; Cheng Xun was transferred to Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Co-director of the Chancellery, and moved to military governor of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuanmin was promoted to General-in-Chief of the Right Brave Guards. Cheng Xun became acting Left Vice Director, chancellor, and was posted as military governor of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 於是宰相路巖、韋保衡劾承訓討賊逗撓，貪虜獲，不時上功。

translations.literal: Then chief ministers Lu Yan and Wei Baoheng impeached Cheng Xun for dilatory pursuit of the bandits, greed for captives and loot, and failure to report victories promptly.
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers Lu Yan and Wei Baoheng then accused Cheng Xun of dragging his feet against the rebels, hoarding booty, and delaying battle reports.

sentences.zh: 貶蜀王傅，分司東都。

translations.literal: He was demoted to tutor to the Prince of Shu and assigned to the Eastern Capital branch office.
translations.idiomatic: He was reduced to tutor of the Prince of Shu and sent to idle duty in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 再貶恩州司馬。

translations.literal: He was demoted again to libationer in En prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: A second demotion made him libationer at Enzhou.

sentences.zh: 僖宗立，授左千牛衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong acceded, he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong took the throne, he was made General-in-Chief of the Left Thousand-Ox Guard.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十六。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 承訓子 傳業子傳業，嘗從父征伐，終鄜坊節度使。

translations.literal: Cheng Xun's son Chuan Ye—Chuan Ye had accompanied his father on campaign and ended as military governor of Bian and Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xun's son Chuan Ye fought with his father from youth and ended his career as military governor of Bian-Fang.

sentences.zh: = 李洧 =

translations.literal: = Li Wei =
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei

sentences.zh: 李洧者，淄青節度使正己從父兄也。

translations.literal: Li Wei was the older paternal cousin of Zheng Ji, military governor of Ziqing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei was the elder cousin of Zheng Ji, military governor of Ziqing.

sentences.zh: 始，署徐州刺史。

translations.literal: At first he was appointed prefect of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was first named prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 建中初，正己卒，子納叛，攻宋州，洧挈州自歸，加兼御史大夫，封潮陽郡王，實封戶二百，充招諭使。

translations.literal: At the start of Jianzhong, Zheng Ji died; his son Na rebelled and attacked Song prefecture. Wei brought his prefecture over to the throne; he was additionally made Censor-in-Chief, enfeoffed as Prince of Chaoyang with two hundred taxable households, and appointed commissioner for recruitment and persuasion.
translations.idiomatic: In the opening years of Jianzhong, Zheng Ji died and his son Na rebelled against Songzhou. Wei surrendered his prefecture to the court, received the additional title Censor-in-Chief, was enfeoffed Prince of Chaoyang with two hundred households, and named commissioner to win others back to the throne.

sentences.zh: 初，洧遣巡官崔程入朝，且白宰相：「徐州不足獨抗賊，得海、沂為節度，可與成功。

translations.literal: Early on Wei sent touring officer Cui Cheng to court with a message to the chief ministers: "Xuzhou alone cannot stand against the bandits; if Hai and Yi were made a military governorship, success would be possible.
translations.idiomatic: Wei had earlier sent touring officer Cui Cheng to court to tell the chancellors: "Xuzhou cannot fight the rebels alone—we need a governorship covering Hai and Yi to finish the job.

sentences.zh: 洧素與二州刺史有約，且不肯為賊守。

translations.literal: Wei had long had an agreement with the two prefects, and they would not hold out for the rebels."
translations.idiomatic: Wei already had a pact with those two prefects, who refused to serve the rebels."

sentences.zh: 」程先咨張鎰，而盧杞怒不先白，故洧請中格。

translations.literal: Cui Cheng first consulted Zhang Yi, but Lu Qi was angry that he had not been informed first, so Wei's request was blocked midway.
translations.idiomatic: Cui had consulted Zhang Yi first; Lu Qi, furious at being bypassed, blocked Wei's proposal.

sentences.zh: 及納攻徐，劉玄佐與諸將擊退之。

translations.literal: When Na attacked Xu, Liu Xuanzuo and the generals beat him back.
translations.idiomatic: When Na assaulted Xuzhou, Liu Xuanzuo and his generals drove him off.

sentences.zh: 既賊方張，乃加洧徐海沂密觀察使。

translations.literal: Once the rebels were at their height, Wei was additionally made governor of Xu, Hai, Yi, and Mi.
translations.idiomatic: With the rebellion in full swing, Wei was made governor over Xu, Hai, Yi, and Mi.

sentences.zh: 時海、密為賊守，不受命，洧未有以取之。

translations.literal: At the time Hai and Mi were held for the rebels and would not accept orders; Wei had no means to take them.
translations.idiomatic: Hai and Mi were still held by rebels who ignored his commission, and Wei had no way to seize them.

sentences.zh: 遷檢校戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to acting Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to acting Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 會疽發背，少間，肩輿過市，市人叫歡，洧驚，疽潰卒，贈尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: A carbuncle broke out on his back; shortly afterward, carried in a sedan chair through the market, the townspeople shouted in celebration. Startled, Wei died when the sore burst; posthumously he was granted Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: A back abscess opened; soon after, borne through the market in a litter, he was startled by the crowds cheering and died when the wound burst. He was posthumously made Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 以洧將高承宗代之。

translations.literal: Wei's general Gao Chengzong was appointed in his place.
translations.idiomatic: His general Gao Chengzong replaced him.

sentences.zh: 洧弟 淡其弟淡，險人也，恥居下，陰約納攻徐為內應，並說滕將翟濟，濟執以聞。

translations.literal: Wei's younger brother Dan—Dan was a dangerous man, ashamed to rank below others—secretly plotted with Na to attack Xu from within and also persuaded Teng's general Zhai Ji; Ji seized him and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's younger brother Dan—a scheming man who hated subordinate rank—secretly plotted with Na to open Xuzhou from within and tried to win over Teng's general Zhai Ji, who arrested him and reported the plot.

sentences.zh: 擢濟沂州刺史。

translations.literal: Ji was promoted to prefect of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Ji was promoted to prefect of Yi.

sentences.zh: 召淡入京師，以洧赦不罪。

translations.literal: Dan was summoned to the capital; because of Wei he was pardoned and not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Dan was summoned to the capital but spared on account of Wei.

sentences.zh: = 劉澭 =

translations.literal: = Liu Yong =
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yong

sentences.zh: 劉澭，盧龍節度使怦之次子，濟母弟也。

translations.literal: Liu Yong was the second son of Peng, military governor of Lulong, and a younger maternal brother of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yong was the second son of Lulong governor Peng and a younger maternal brother of Ji.

sentences.zh: 涉書史，有材武，好施愛士，能得人死力。

translations.literal: He studied books and histories, had talent and martial skill, loved to bestow favors and cherish officers, and could win men to give their lives.
translations.idiomatic: He was versed in history, skilled in arms, generous with his officers, and could bind men to die for him.

sentences.zh: 始事朱滔，常陳君臣大分，裁抑其兇。

translations.literal: He first served Zhu Tao, often expounding the great divide between ruler and subject and curbing his violence.
translations.idiomatic: He began under Zhu Tao, repeatedly invoking the bounds of loyalty and restraining his brutality.

sentences.zh: 及怦得幽州，不三月病且死，澭侍湯液未嘗離，輒以父命召濟於莫州，濟嗣總軍事，故德澭之讓，以為瀛州刺史，有如不諱，許代己。

translations.literal: When Peng obtained You prefecture, within three months he fell ill and was near death. Yong attended his medicaments without leaving; he repeatedly summoned Ji from Mo prefecture by his father's order. Ji succeeded to overall command and therefore esteemed Yong's yielding; he made him prefect of Ying, with the understanding that if misfortune should come, Yong would succeed him.
translations.idiomatic: Peng won Youzhou but within three months lay dying. Yong never left his bedside and sent repeatedly for Ji in Mozhou by their father's command. Ji took command and, grateful for Yong's deferral, made him prefect of Ying with a promise to succeed him if death came.

sentences.zh: 久之，濟自用其子為副大使，澭不能無恨，因請以所部為天子戍隴，悉發其兵千五百馳歸京師，無一卒敢違令者。

translations.literal: After a long time Ji appointed his own son deputy commissioner; Yong could not but resent it, and therefore requested that his command garrison Long for the Son of Heaven, mustering all his troops—one thousand five hundred—and galloping back to the capital; not a single soldier dared disobey the order.
translations.idiomatic: In time Ji installed his own son as deputy heir; Yong nursed a grudge and asked to lead his troops—fifteen hundred men—to garrison Long for the throne. They rode to the capital and not one soldier disobeyed.

sentences.zh: 德宗甚寵之，拜秦州刺史，屯普潤。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong greatly favored him, appointing him prefect of Qin and garrisoning him at Purun.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong favored him warmly, made him prefect of Qin, and stationed him at Purun.

sentences.zh: 軍中不設音樂。

translations.literal: In the army no music was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He banned music in camp.

sentences.zh: 士卒病，親存問所欲，不幸死，哭之。

translations.literal: When soldiers fell ill, he personally inquired after their needs; when they died despite care, he wept for them.
translations.idiomatic: Sick soldiers he visited himself; when they died he mourned them openly.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立，方士羅令則詣澭營，妄言廢立以動澭，命系之，辭曰：「吾之黨甚眾，公無囚我，約大行梓宮發兵，無不濟。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xianzong acceded, the magician Luo Lingze came to Yong's camp and recklessly spoke of deposing and enthroning to move Yong; Yong ordered him bound. Luo said in his defense: "My faction is very numerous—you must not imprison me; we have agreed that when the late emperor's coffin moves we shall raise troops—nothing can fail.
translations.idiomatic: At Xianzong's accession the magician Luo Lingze came to Yong's camp spinning plots of deposition. Yong had him seized. Luo protested: "My allies are many—do not bind me. We pledged to rise when the late emperor's coffin departs; it cannot fail.

sentences.zh: 」澭械送闕下，殺之。

translations.literal: " Yong sent him under guard to the capital and had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: Yong shipped him to the capital in irons and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 錄功，號其軍曰保義。

translations.literal: Recording the achievement, his army was titled Preserving Righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: For the service his corps was named Preserving Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 蕃戎畏懾，不敢入寇。

translations.literal: Barbarians feared and did not dare raid.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal enemies feared him and stopped raiding.

sentences.zh: 常愾然有復河湟誌，屢為朝廷言之，未見省。

translations.literal: He often burned with the resolve to recover the Hehuang region, spoke of it repeatedly to the court, but was never heeded.
translations.idiomatic: He ached to recover the Hehuang frontier and pleaded with the court again and again, but no one listened.

sentences.zh: 封累彭城郡公。

translations.literal: Through successive enfeoffments he became Duke of Pengcheng commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed Duke of Pengcheng in cumulative honors.

sentences.zh: 及病，籍士馬求代。

translations.literal: When he fell ill, he registered his men and horses and requested a replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Falling ill, he mustered rolls of men and horses and asked to be relieved.

sentences.zh: 既還，卒於道，年四十九，贈尚書右僕射，謚曰景。

translations.literal: Having returned, he died on the road at age forty-nine; posthumously granted Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the homeward march at forty-nine, posthumously made Right Vice Director with the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: = 田弘正 =

translations.literal: = Tian Hongzheng =
translations.idiomatic: Tian Hongzheng

sentences.zh: 田弘正，字安道。

translations.literal: Tian Hongzheng, style name Andao.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Hongzheng, courtesy name Andao.

sentences.zh: 父廷玠，尚儒學，不樂軍旅，與承嗣為從昆弟，仕為平舒丞，遷樂壽、清池、束城、河間四縣令，以治稱。

translations.literal: His father Tingjie valued Confucian learning and did not delight in military affairs. He and Chengsi were paternal cousins; Tingjie served as assistant magistrate of Pingshu, then magistrate of four counties—Yueshou, Qingchi, Dongcheng, and Hejian—and was famed for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tingjie was a Confucian scholar who shunned soldiery. A cousin of Chengsi, he served as magistrate of Pingshu and then of Yueshou, Qingchi, Dongcheng, and Hejian, winning fame for his administration.

sentences.zh: 遷滄州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Cang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to prefect of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 李寶臣、朱滔與承嗣不協，合兵圍滄州，廷玠固守連年，食雖盡無叛者。

translations.literal: Li Baochen, Zhu Tao, and Chengsi were at odds; they united armies and besieged Cang prefecture. Tingjie held firm for years; though food ran out, none rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baochen and Zhu Tao, feuding with Chengsi, jointly besieged Cangzhou. Tingjie held out for years; even when stores were gone, no man turned traitor.

sentences.zh: 朝廷嘉其節，徙相州。

translations.literal: The court praised his steadfastness and moved him to Xiang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The court honored his constancy and transferred him to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 承嗣盜磁、相，廷玠無所回染。

translations.literal: Chengsi seized Ci and Xiang prefectures, but Tingjie was not tainted in any way.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengsi seized Ci and Xiang, Tingjie kept himself untouched.

sentences.zh: 及悅代立，忌廷玠之正，召為節度副使。

translations.literal: When Yue succeeded to power, jealous of Tingjie's rectitude, he summoned him as deputy military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue took over he resented Tingjie's integrity and summoned him as deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 廷玠至，讓悅曰：「而承伯父緒業，當守朝廷法度以保富貴，何苦與恒、鄆為叛臣？

translations.literal: When Tingjie arrived he reproached Yue: "You inherit your uncle's position—you ought to keep the court's laws to preserve wealth and rank. Why suffer alongside Heng and Yun as rebel ministers?
translations.idiomatic: Tingjie upbraided Yue: "You stand in your uncle's place—you should uphold the dynasty's law and keep your fortune. Why join Heng and Yun as traitors?

sentences.zh: 自兵興來，叛天子能完宗族者誰邪？

translations.literal: Since the wars began, who among those who rebelled against the Son of Heaven has preserved his clan whole?"
translations.idiomatic: "Since these wars began, which rebel has kept his whole house alive?"

sentences.zh: 而誌不悛，盍殺我，無令我見田氏血汙人刀也！

translations.literal: Since your heart will not repent, better kill me—do not make me see Tian blood staining another's blade!"
translations.idiomatic: "If you will not turn back, kill me now—don't make me watch Tian blood on another man's sword!"

sentences.zh: 」遂稱疾不出。

translations.literal: He then pleaded illness and did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and refused to leave his house.

sentences.zh: 悅過謝之，杜門不納，憤而卒。

translations.literal: Yue came in person to apologize; Tingjie shut his door and would not admit him, and died in anger.
translations.idiomatic: Yue came to apologize in person; Tingjie barred his door and died in outrage.

sentences.zh: 弘正幼通兵法，善騎射，承嗣愛之，以為必興吾宗，名之曰興。

translations.literal: Hongzheng from youth mastered military arts and excelled at mounted archery; Chengsi loved him, thinking he would surely revive our clan, and named him Xing ("Rise").
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng learned strategy young and shot well from horseback; Chengsi adored him, believing he would restore the clan, and named him Xing—"Prosper."

sentences.zh: 季安時，為衙內兵馬使、同節度副使，封沂國公。

translations.literal: Under Ji'an he was inner-gate horse commissioner and concurrent deputy military commissioner, enfeoffed Duke of Yi state.
translations.idiomatic: Under Ji'an he served as inner-gate horse commissioner and deputy commissioner, enfeoffed Duke of Yi.

sentences.zh: 季安侈汰，銳殺罰，弘正從容規切，軍中賴之，翕然歸重。

translations.literal: Ji'an was extravagant and excessive, keen on punishments and executions; Hongzheng calmly advised and admonished; the army relied on him and all turned to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji'an lived lavishly and punished harshly; Hongzheng counseled him steadily, and the troops looked to Hongzheng with growing respect.

sentences.zh: 季安內忌，出為臨清鎮將，欲因罪誅之。

translations.literal: Ji'an inwardly resented him and posted him as garrison commander at Linqing, intending to punish him on a charge.
translations.idiomatic: Ji'an grew jealous and sent him to command Linqing, planning to destroy him on some pretext.

sentences.zh: 弘正陽痹痼，臥家不出，乃免。

translations.literal: Hongzheng feigned chronic paralysis, lay at home and did not go out, and thereby escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng played crippled with a chronic ailment, stayed bedridden at home, and survived.

sentences.zh: 季安死，子懷諫襲節度，召還舊職。

translations.literal: When Ji'an died, his son Huaijian succeeded to the commission and recalled Hongzheng to his former post.
translations.idiomatic: Ji'an died; his son Huaijian took command and restored Hongzheng to his old post.

sentences.zh: 懷諫委政於家奴蔣士則，措置不平，眾怒，咸曰：「兵馬使吾帥也。

translations.literal: Huaijian entrusted government to the household slave Jiang Shize, whose arrangements were unjust; the troops were enraged and all said: "The horse commissioner is our commander."
translations.idiomatic: Huaijian handed power to his house steward Jiang Shize, who ruled unfairly. The soldiers fumed: "Our horse commissioner is the man who should lead us."

sentences.zh: 」牙兵即詣其家迎之，弘正拒不納，眾嘩於門，弘正出，眾拜之，脅還府，弘正頓於地，度不免，即令於軍曰：「爾屬不以吾不肖，使主軍，今與公等約，能聽命否？

translations.literal: The guard soldiers at once went to his home to welcome him; Hongzheng refused to admit them. The crowd clamored at the gate; Hongzheng came out, the crowd bowed to him and forced him back to headquarters. Hongzheng collapsed to the ground; seeing he could not escape, he addressed the army: "You would not consider me unworthy and would have me command the army—now I make a pact with you all: will you obey orders?"
translations.idiomatic: The guard troops marched to his house to install him; Hongzheng would not open the door. They shouted at the gate until he came out; they bowed and dragged him back to headquarters. He sank to the ground, saw there was no escape, and told the army: "You mean to make me your commander—then hear my terms: will you obey?"

sentences.zh: 」皆曰：「惟公命。

translations.literal: All said: "Only as you command."
translations.idiomatic: "Whatever you say," they answered.

sentences.zh: 」因曰：「吾欲守天子法，舉六州版籍請吏於朝，茍天子未命，敢有請吾旗節者死，殺人及掠人者死。

translations.literal: He then said: "I wish to keep the Son of Heaven's law, submit the registers of the six prefectures and request officials from court; if the Son of Heaven has not yet appointed, whoever asks for my banner and commission dies; whoever kills or plunders people dies."
translations.idiomatic: "I will uphold imperial law," he said. "We will surrender the six prefectures' registers and ask the court for officials. Until the throne appoints a governor, anyone who demands my seal and banner dies—and anyone who kills or loots dies too."

sentences.zh: 」皆曰：「諾。

translations.literal: All said: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: "Agreed," they said.

sentences.zh: 」遂到府，殺士則及支黨十餘人。

translations.literal: He then went to headquarters and killed Shize and more than ten of his faction.
translations.idiomatic: He entered headquarters and executed Shize and more than ten of his followers.

sentences.zh: 於是圖魏、博、相、衛、貝、澶之地，籍其入以獻，不敢署僚屬，而待王官。

translations.literal: Thereupon he mapped the lands of Wei, Bo, Xiang, Wei, Bei, and Chan, registered their revenues and presented them, dared not appoint staff, and awaited court officials.
translations.idiomatic: He surveyed Wei, Bo, Xiang, Wei, Bei, and Chan, listed their revenues for the throne, appointed no officials of his own, and waited for the court to send them.

sentences.zh: 先時，諸將出屯，質妻子，裏民不得相往來。

translations.literal: Previously, when generals went out to garrison, they left wives and children as hostages; commoners were not permitted to visit one another.
translations.idiomatic: Before, generals on campaign left their families as hostages and common people were forbidden to visit one another.

sentences.zh: 弘正悉除其禁，聽民通饋謝慶吊。

translations.literal: Hongzheng entirely removed these prohibitions and allowed the people to exchange gifts and pay calls for congratulations and mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng lifted every restriction and let people visit freely for gifts, congratulations, and funerals.

sentences.zh: 服玩僭侈者，即日徹毀之。

translations.literal: Those whose dress and ornaments exceeded their rank—on the same day he had them dismantled and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone flaunting forbidden luxuries had them stripped and destroyed that same day.

sentences.zh: 承嗣時，正寢華顯，弘正避不敢居，更就采訪使堂皇聽事。

translations.literal: In Chengsi's time the main hall had been splendid; Hongzheng avoided it and did not dare dwell there, moving instead to the investigating commissioner's public hall for audiences.
translations.idiomatic: Chengsi's hall had been opulent; Hongzheng refused to live there and held court in the investigating commissioner's plainer hall.

sentences.zh: 幽、恒、鄆、蔡大懼，遣客鐫說鉤染，弘正皆拒遣之。

translations.literal: You, Heng, Yun, and Cai were greatly afraid; they sent agents to engrave persuasions and win him over—Hongzheng all refused and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: The governors of You, Heng, Yun, and Cai were terrified and sent agents to flatter and bribe him; Hongzheng turned every one away.

sentences.zh: 憲宗美其誠，詔檢校工部尚書，充魏博節度使。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong praised his sincerity; an edict appointed him acting Minister of Works and military governor of Weibo.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong praised his loyalty and made him acting Minister of Works and military governor of Weibo.

sentences.zh: 又遣司封郎中知制誥裴度宣慰，賚其軍錢百五十萬緡，六州民給復一年，赦見囚，存問高年、惸獨、廢疾不能自存者。

translations.literal: The court also sent Secretariat Director and drafter of edicts Pei Du to proclaim consolation, bestowing on the army one million five hundred thousand strings of cash, granting the six prefectures' people tax relief for one year, pardoning prisoners in custody, and inquiring after the aged, the orphaned and alone, and the disabled who could not support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Secretariat Director Pei Du to announce imperial favor: one million five hundred thousand strings for the army, a year's tax remission for the six prefectures, amnesty for prisoners, and relief for the aged, the alone, and the disabled.

sentences.zh: 度明辯，具陳朝廷厚意，弘正不覺自失，乃深相結納，奉上益謹。

translations.literal: Du was clear in argument and fully set forth the court's generous intent; Hongzheng unconsciously felt himself diminished and therefore bonded deeply with him, serving the throne with greater care.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du spoke with force and laid out the throne's goodwill; Hongzheng felt himself humbled and drew close to him, serving the court with redoubled care.

sentences.zh: 復請度遍行其部，宣示天子恩詔。

translations.literal: He again asked Du to tour the whole of his territory and proclaim the Son of Heaven's gracious edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He asked Pei Du to tour the whole command and read the emperor's edicts of grace.

sentences.zh: 因令節度僉謀布衣崔歡奉表陳謝，且言：「天寶以來，山東奧壤，化為戎墟，官封世襲，刑賞自出，國家含垢，垂六十年。

translations.literal: He then had the military commissioner's adviser, commoner Cui Huan, submit a memorial of thanks, saying: "Since Tianbao, the rich lands east of the mountains have become a wasteland of war; office and fief passed by inheritance, punishments and rewards issued from private hands—the state swallowed the shame for nearly sixty years.
translations.idiomatic: He had his adviser, the commoner Cui Huan, submit a memorial of thanks: "Since Tianbao the heartland east of the mountains has been battleground; offices and fiefs passed father to son, punishments and rewards came from private hands—and the throne bore that shame for nearly sixty years.

sentences.zh: 臣若假天之齡，奉陛下宸算，冀道揚太和，洗濯偽風，然後退歸丘園，避賢者路，死不恨。

translations.literal: If Heaven grants me years, to follow Your Majesty's plans, I hope to spread great harmony, wash away false ways—and then retire to my hills, yielding the road to worthier men; I would die without regret."
translations.idiomatic: "If Heaven lengthens my days, I will follow Your Majesty's design, restore peace, and scour away these false ways—then withdraw to my home and make way for better men. I could die content."

sentences.zh: 」制詔褒答，且賜今名，錫與踵塗。

translations.literal: An edict answered in praise and moreover granted his present name, bestowing gifts in succession.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised him in reply, granted his present name Hongzheng, and showered him with gifts.

sentences.zh: 天子討蔡，弘正遣子布以兵三千進戰，數有功。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven campaigned against Cai, Hongzheng sent his son Bu with three thousand troops to advance and fight, repeatedly achieving merit.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne attacked Cai, Hongzheng sent his son Bu with three thousand men to the front; they won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 李師道疑其襲己，不敢顯助蔡，故元濟失援，王師得致誅焉。

translations.literal: Li Shidao suspected he would strike at himself and did not dare openly aid Cai; therefore Yuanji lost support and the imperial army was able to bring about his execution.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shidao feared a strike against himself and dared not aid Cai openly, so Yuanji lost support and the imperial army finished him.

sentences.zh: 王承宗叛，詔弘正以全師壓境，破其眾南宮，承宗懼，歸窮於弘正，弘正表諸朝，遂獻德、棣二州以謝，納二子為質。

translations.literal: Wang Chengzong rebelled; an edict ordered Hongzheng to press the border with his full army and break his force at Nangong. Chengzong was afraid, threw himself on Hongzheng's mercy; Hongzheng memorialized the court, and Chengzong thereupon offered De and Di prefectures in apology and sent two sons as hostages.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengzong rebelled; Hongzheng was ordered to mass his full army on the border and routed him at Nangong. Chengzong, terrified, appealed to Hongzheng, who petitioned the court; Chengzong surrendered De and Di and sent two sons as hostages.

sentences.zh: 俄而李師道拒命，詔弘正與宣武等五節度兵進討。

translations.literal: Soon Li Shidao defied orders; an edict ordered Hongzheng and five other military governors of Xuanwu and elsewhere to advance and attack.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li Shidao defied the throne; Hongzheng joined five other governors, including Xuanwu, in a joint campaign.

sentences.zh: 弘正自揚劉度河，距鄆四十里堅壁；

translations.literal: Hongzheng himself crossed the river at Yangliu and encamped forty li from Yun, holding a fortified camp;
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng crossed the Yangliu ford and entrenched forty li from Yun;

sentences.zh: 師道大將劉悟率精兵屯河東。

translations.literal: Shidao's great general Liu Wu led elite troops garrisoned east of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao's chief general Liu Wu held the east bank with picked troops.

sentences.zh: 戰陽谷，再遇再北，斬萬餘級，賊勢蹙。

translations.literal: They fought at Yanggu; twice they met and twice the rebels were beaten; more than ten thousand heads were cut; the bandit force was pressed hard.
translations.idiomatic: At Yanggu they clashed twice and the rebels lost both times; more than ten thousand were killed and the enemy was cornered.

sentences.zh: 悟乃反兵，斬師道首，詣弘正降，取十有二州以獻。

translations.literal: Wu then turned his army, beheaded Shidao's head, came to Hongzheng to surrender, and presented twelve prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Wu then mutinied, cut off Shidao's head, surrendered to Hongzheng, and turned over twelve prefectures.

sentences.zh: 初，悟既平賊，大張飲軍中，凡三日，設角觝戲，引魏博使至廷以為歡，悟盱衡攘臂助其決，坐中皆憚悟勇。

translations.literal: At first, once Wu had pacified the bandits, he held a great feast in the army for three days in all, set up grappling contests, and summoned the Weibo envoy to the hall for merriment; Wu glared and flexed his arms to help decide the bouts, and all present feared Wu's valor.
translations.idiomatic: After the victory Wu feasted the army for three days, staged wrestling matches, and invited the Weibo envoy to watch; he glared and cheered the bouts, and everyone feared his ferocity.

sentences.zh: 客有白弘正者，弘正曰：「鄆士疲於戰，瘡者未起，悟當恤亡吊乏，尉士大夫心，奈何取快目前邪？

translations.literal: A guest reported this to Hongzheng; Hongzheng said: "The men of Yun are weary from war; the wounded have not yet risen—Wu ought to comfort the dead and succor the needy, to soothe the hearts of officers and gentry. Why seek present amusement?
translations.idiomatic: Someone told Hongzheng, who said: "Yun's soldiers are exhausted; the wounded are still abed. Wu should mourn the dead and aid the destitute to win over the gentry—not indulge himself for a moment's pleasure.

sentences.zh: 吾奉詔按軍，伺悟去就，今知其無能為也。

translations.literal: I have received an edict to inspect the army and watch Wu's intentions; now I know he is incapable of action.
translations.idiomatic: "I was ordered to oversee the army and watch Liu Wu," he said. "Now I see he cannot do anything."

sentences.zh: 」既而詔悟為義成軍節度使，狼狽上道，時稱知悟之明。

translations.literal: Soon an edict appointed Wu military governor of Yicheng; he set out in disarray, and at the time people praised Hongzheng's clear judgment of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then made Liu Wu governor of Yicheng; he left in disorder, and contemporaries praised Hongzheng for reading him correctly.

sentences.zh: 以功加弘正檢校司徒、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: For his merit Hongzheng was additionally made Acting Minister of Works and Co-director of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: For his service Hongzheng was made acting Minister of Works and chancellor.

sentences.zh: 是歲來朝，對麟德殿，眷勞殊等；

translations.literal: That year he came to court and was received at Linde Hall with exceptional favor;
translations.idiomatic: That year he came to court, was received at Linde Hall, and honored beyond the usual;

sentences.zh: 引見僚佐將校二百餘人，皆有班賜；

translations.literal: more than two hundred staff officers and commanders were introduced and all received ranked gifts;
translations.idiomatic: more than two hundred aides and commanders were presented and all received graded rewards;

sentences.zh: 進兼侍中，實封戶三百；

translations.literal: he was further made concurrent Palace Attendant with three hundred taxable households;
translations.idiomatic: he was further made Palace Attendant with three hundred taxable households;

sentences.zh: 擢其兄融為太子賓客、東都留司。

translations.literal: his elder brother Rong was promoted to Mentor of the Heir Apparent and left in charge at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: his elder brother Rong was made Mentor of the Heir Apparent and left at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 弘正數上表固請留闕下，帝勞曰：「昨韓弘以疾辭不就軍，朕既從之矣，今卿復爾，我不應違。

translations.literal: Hongzheng repeatedly submitted memorials firmly requesting to remain at court; the emperor consoled him, saying: "Yesterday Han Hong declined the army on grounds of illness and I granted it—now you do the same, and I should not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng repeatedly asked to stay at court. The emperor said: "Han Hong just declined command on grounds of illness and I let him go—you ask the same, and I cannot refuse.

sentences.zh: 但魏人樂卿之政，四鄰畏卿之威，為朕長城，又安用辭？

translations.literal: But the people of Wei delight in your governance, and the four neighboring provinces fear your authority—be my long wall; why insist on declining?"
translations.idiomatic: But Wei loves your rule and the borders fear your strength. Be my bulwark—why refuse?"

sentences.zh: 」弘正遂還。

translations.literal: Hongzheng then returned.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng went back.

sentences.zh: 常欲變山東承襲舊風，故悉遣子姓仕朝廷，帝皆擢任之，朱紫滿門，榮冠當時。

translations.literal: He often wished to change the old custom of hereditary succession east of the mountains, and therefore sent all his sons and clansmen to serve at court; the emperor promoted them all—purple and scarlet filled the household, glory unmatched in the age.
translations.idiomatic: He wanted to break the hereditary custom of the northeast and sent every son and kinsman to serve at court; the throne promoted them all until purple and scarlet robes filled the house—the envy of the age.

sentences.zh: 穆宗立，王承元以成德軍請帥，帝詔弘正兼中書令，為節度使。

translations.literal: When Muzong acceded, Wang Chengyuan offered the Chengde army to the throne; the emperor ordered Hongzheng additionally made Chief Director of the Chancellery and military governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Muzong took the throne, Wang Chengyuan offered Chengde to the court; Hongzheng was made chief director and military governor.

sentences.zh: 弘正以新與鎮人戰，有父兄怨，取魏兵二千自衛，入其軍。

translations.literal: Hongzheng had recently fought the Zhen troops and there were grievances from fathers and brothers; he took two thousand Wei soldiers as escort and entered their army.
translations.idiomatic: He had just fought the Zhen troops and many bore blood grudges; he took two thousand Wei soldiers as escort into their camp.

sentences.zh: 時天子賜錢一百萬緡，不時至，軍有怨言，弘正親加撫喻乃安。

translations.literal: At the time the Son of Heaven had bestowed one million strings of cash, which did not arrive on time; the army murmured in complaint, and Hongzheng personally soothed and reassured them before they settled.
translations.idiomatic: The throne had promised a million strings of cash that arrived late; the troops grumbled until Hongzheng calmed them in person.

sentences.zh: 仍請留魏兵為紀綱，以持眾心，度支崔倰吝其稟，沮卻之。

translations.literal: He still requested to keep Wei troops as discipline to hold the troops' hearts; Fiscal Commissioner Cui Jun begrudged their rations and blocked it.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to keep Wei troops as a guard force; Fiscal Commissioner Cui Jun, stingy with their pay, refused.

sentences.zh: 長慶元年七月，歸衛卒於魏，是月軍亂，並家屬將吏三百餘人皆遇害，年五十八。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Changqing he returned the guard soldiers to Wei; that same month the army mutinied, and more than three hundred kin, staff, and officers were all killed; he was fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Changqing 1 he sent the Wei guards home; that month the army mutinied and killed him with more than three hundred kin, staff, and officers. He was fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 帝聞震悼，冊贈太尉，謚曰忠湣。

translations.literal: The emperor, hearing, was shaken with grief; posthumously he was enfeoffed Grand Preceptor with posthumous title Zhongmin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was stricken with grief and posthumously made him Grand Preceptor with the posthumous name Zhongmin.

sentences.zh: 弘正幼孤，事融甚謹，軍中嘗分曹習射，弘正註矢聯中，融退，抶怒之，故當季安猜暴時能自全。

translations.literal: Hongzheng was orphaned young and served Rong with great care. Once in the army they practiced archery by squad; Hongzheng scored successive hits with marked arrows; Rong withdrew and angrily flogged him—therefore during Ji'an's suspicious brutality he could preserve himself.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Hongzheng served his brother Rong meticulously. During squad archery he scored every marked shot; Rong withdrew and beat him for it—discipline that helped him survive Ji'an's suspicious reign.

sentences.zh: 及為軍中推迫，融不悅曰：「爾竟不自晦，取禍之道也。

translations.literal: When the army forced him forward, Rong said unhappily: "You truly will not hide your light—that is the way to invite disaster."
translations.idiomatic: When the troops pressed him to lead, Rong warned: "You refuse to keep your head down—that is how men invite ruin."

sentences.zh: 」朝廷知其友愛，詔拜相州刺史，賜金紫，不欲其相遠也。

translations.literal: The court knew their brotherly love and ordered Rong appointed prefect of Xiang, bestowing gold and purple so they would not be far apart.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing their bond, the court made Rong prefect of Xiang with gold and purple rank so the brothers would stay near each other.

sentences.zh: 弘正性忠孝，好功名，起樓聚書萬餘卷，通《春秋左氏》，與賓屬講論終日，客為著《沂公史例》行於世。

translations.literal: Hongzheng was loyal and filial by nature, loved merit and fame, built a tower and gathered more than ten thousand volumes, mastered the Zuo Commentary to the Spring and Autumn Annals, and debated with guests and staff all day; a guest wrote Records of Duke Yi's Historiography, which circulated in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal and ambitious, Hongzheng built a library of ten thousand volumes, mastered the Zuo Commentary, and debated history with guests all day—a guest's Records of Duke Yi circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 弘正之禍也，其判官劉茂復獨免，士相戒曰：「是人議事盡忠，遇吾等信，敢幹其家者共殺之。

translations.literal: At Hongzheng's disaster his aide Liu Maofu alone escaped; soldiers warned one another: "This man deliberates with full loyalty and treats us in good faith—whoever dares harm his household, let us kill him together."
translations.idiomatic: When Hongzheng fell, only his aide Liu Maofu was spared. The soldiers swore: "He served us faithfully—harm his family and we kill you."
So they swore.

sentences.zh: 弘正子布、群、牟。

translations.literal: Hongzheng's sons were Bu, Qun, and Mou.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Bu, Qun, and Mou.

sentences.zh: 弘正子 布布字敦禮，幼機悟。

translations.literal: Hongzheng's son Bu—Bu, style name Dunli, was clever from childhood.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzheng's son Bu, courtesy name Dunli, was precocious as a boy.

sentences.zh: 弘正戍臨清，布知季安且危，密白父，請以眾歸朝，弘正奇之。

translations.literal: When Hongzheng garrisoned Linqing, Bu knew Ji'an was near ruin; he secretly told his father to bring the troops over to the throne; Hongzheng marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: While Hongzheng held Linqing, Bu saw Ji'an was doomed and secretly urged his father to surrender the troops to the throne; Hongzheng was astonished.

sentences.zh: 及得魏，使布總親兵。

translations.literal: Once he obtained Wei, he had Bu command the personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held Wei, he put Bu in command of his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 王師誅蔡，以軍隸嚴綬，屯唐州。

translations.literal: When the imperial army executed Cai, the troops were placed under Yan Shou and garrisoned at Tang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army took Cai, his troops were assigned to Yan Shou and stationed at Tangzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝以布大臣子，或有罪，且橈法，弘正請以董畹代，而士卒愛布願留，帝乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Bu was a great minister's son and might commit some offense yet still bend the law, Hongzheng requested Dong Wan replace him; but the soldiers loved Bu and wished him to remain, and the emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing favoritism toward a minister's son, Hongzheng asked Dong Wan to replace Bu; the troops wanted Bu to stay and the emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 凡十八戰，破淩雲柵，下郾城，以功授御史中丞。

translations.literal: In all eighteen battles he broke the Lingyun palisade and took Yancheng; for merit he was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In eighteen battles he stormed the Lingyun palisade and took Yancheng, earning appointment as Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 裴度輕出觀兵沱口，賊將董重質以奇兵掩擊，布伏騎數百突出薄之，諸軍繼至，賊驚引還。

translations.literal: Pei Du lightly went out to inspect the troops at Tuokou; the bandit general Dong Chongzhi struck with surprise troops; Bu's hidden cavalry of several hundred burst out and pressed them; the armies followed and the bandits withdrew in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du rode out to inspect Tuokou; Dong Chongzhi ambushed him. Bu's hidden cavalry charged, the main force followed, and the rebels fled.

sentences.zh: 蔡平，入為左金吾衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Cai was pacified he entered court as general of the Left Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: After Cai fell he entered court as general of the Left Golden Guard.

sentences.zh: 諫官嘗論事帝前，同列將麾卻之，布止曰：「使天子容直臣，毋輕進。

translations.literal: Once when remonstrating officials debated before the emperor, colleagues were about to wave them back; Bu stopped them, saying: "Let the Son of Heaven hear straight counsel—do not dismiss them lightly."
translations.idiomatic: When censors debated before the throne and colleagues tried to wave them off, Bu said: "Let the emperor hear honest words—do not brush them aside."

sentences.zh: 」弘正徙成德，以布為河陽節度使，父子同日受命。

translations.literal: When Hongzheng moved to Chengde, Bu was made military governor of Heyang; father and son received commissions the same day.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongzheng went to Chengde, Bu was made governor of Heyang—father and son commissioned the same day.

sentences.zh: 時韓弘與子公武亦皆領節度，而天下以忠義多田氏。

translations.literal: At the time Han Hong and his son Gongwu also each held a commission, and the realm said loyalty and righteousness abounded in the Tian house.
translations.idiomatic: Han Hong and his son Gongwu held commands at the same time, and the empire praised the Tian family for loyalty.

sentences.zh: 布所至，必省冗將，募戰卒，寬賦勸穡，人皆安之。

translations.literal: Wherever Bu went, he always reduced redundant generals, recruited fighting soldiers, eased levies and encouraged farming; the people all found peace.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Bu served he cut redundant generals, recruited fighters, eased taxes, and encouraged farming—and people prospered.

sentences.zh: 長慶初，徙涇原。

translations.literal: At the start of Changqing he was transferred to Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In early Changqing he was transferred to Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 弘正遇害，魏博節度使李病不能軍，公卿議以魏強而鎮弱，且魏人素德弘正，以布之賢而世其官，可以成功。

translations.literal: After Hongzheng was killed, Wei Bo military governor Li was ill and could not command the army; the chief ministers debated that Wei was strong while Zhen was weak, and the people of Wei had long honored Hongzheng— with Bu's talent succeeding to his office, success could be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: After Hongzheng's murder the Wei Bo governor, Li, was too ill to command. Ministers argued that Wei was strong, Zhen weak, and the Wei troops still revered Hongzheng—with Bu's talent and name, the post could work.

sentences.zh: 穆宗遽召布，解缞拜檢校工部尚書、魏博節度使，乘傳以行。

translations.literal: Muzong hastily summoned Bu, removed mourning garb, and appointed him Acting Minister of Works and military governor of Wei Bo, traveling by post relay.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong summoned Bu at once, had him leave mourning, and made him acting Minister of Works and Wei Bo governor, sending him off by relay.

sentences.zh: 布號泣固辭，不聽；

translations.literal: Bu wailed and firmly declined, but was not heeded;
translations.idiomatic: Bu wept and refused, but the throne would not listen;

sentences.zh: 乃出伎樂，與妻子賓客決曰：「吾不還矣！

translations.literal: he then dismissed musicians and parted from wife, children, and guests, saying: "I will not return!"
translations.idiomatic: he dismissed his musicians and told wife, children, and guests: "I am not coming back!"

sentences.zh: 」未至魏三十里，跣行被發，號哭而入，居堊室，屏節旄。

translations.literal: Thirty li from Wei he walked barefoot with hair loose, wailing as he entered; he dwelt in a mourning hut and put away banner and seal.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty li from Wei he walked barefoot with hair unbound, wailing; he lived in a mourning hut and laid aside banner and seal.

sentences.zh: 凡將士老者，兄事之。

translations.literal: All soldiers who were elderly he treated as elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He treated every veteran soldier as an elder brother.

sentences.zh: 祿奉月百萬，一不入私門，又發家錢十餘萬緡頒士卒。

translations.literal: Salary of one million per month did not enter his private gate; he also disbursed more than one hundred thousand strings from family funds to the troops.
translations.idiomatic: He took none of his million-month salary for himself and paid out more than a hundred thousand strings from family funds to the troops.

sentences.zh: 以牙將史憲誠出麾下可任，乃委以精銳。

translations.literal: Because guard general Shi Xiancheng under his command was capable, he entrusted him with picked troops.
translations.idiomatic: He trusted his guard general Shi Xiancheng with elite troops.

sentences.zh: 時中人屢趣戰，而度支饋餉不繼，布輒以六州租賦給軍。

translations.literal: At the time eunuchs repeatedly pressed for battle, while fiscal supplies did not keep up; Bu then used the six prefectures' land tax to feed the army.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs kept pressing for battle while pay failed to arrive; Bu fed the army from the six prefectures' tax rolls.

sentences.zh: 引兵三萬進屯南宮，破賊二壘。

translations.literal: He led thirty thousand troops forward and encamped at Nangong, breaking two rebel forts.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced thirty thousand men to Nangong and took two rebel forts.

sentences.zh: 於是朱克融據幽州，與王廷湊唇齒。

translations.literal: Thereupon Zhu Kerong held You prefecture and stood cheek by jowl with Wang Tingcou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Kerong held Youzhou and stood shoulder to shoulder with Wang Tingcou.

sentences.zh: 河朔三鎮舊連衡，桀驁自私，而憲誠蓄異志，陰欲乘釁，又魏軍驕，憚格戰，會大雪，師寒糧乏，軍中謗曰：「它日用兵團，粒米盡仰朝廷。

translations.literal: The three Hebei garrisons had long acted in concert, proud and selfish; Xiancheng harbored other designs and secretly wished to seize an opening. The Wei army was arrogant and feared close combat; heavy snow fell, the army was cold and grain was scarce, and in the ranks they slandered: "In other days when troops were deployed, every grain of rice came from the court.
translations.idiomatic: The three Hebei commands had long colluded, proud and selfish. Xiancheng nursed other plans and watched for a chance. The Wei troops were arrogant and feared hard fighting; snow fell, cold and hunger set in, and men grumbled: "When we fought before, every grain came from the court.

sentences.zh: 今六州刮肉與鎮、冀角死生，雖尚書瘠己肥國，魏人何罪？

translations.literal: Now the six prefectures are flayed to fight Zhen and Ji to the death—though the Minister starves himself to fatten the state, what crime have the people of Wei committed?"
translations.idiomatic: Now the six prefectures are stripped bare to fight Zhen and Ji to the death—the Minister may starve himself for the realm, but what have the people of Wei done?"

sentences.zh: 」憲誠得間，因以搖亂。

translations.literal: Xiancheng seized the opening and thereby stirred disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng seized the moment and stirred mutiny.

sentences.zh: 會有詔分布軍合李光顏救深州，兵怒，不肯東，眾遂潰，皆歸憲誠，唯中軍不動。

translations.literal: An edict came ordering Bu's army to join Li Guangyan in rescuing Shen prefecture; the troops were enraged and refused to go east; the host then collapsed, all turning to Xiancheng—only the central army did not move.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Bu to join Li Guangyan at Shenzhou; the troops refused to march east, broke ranks, and rallied to Xiancheng—only the central guard held firm.

sentences.zh: 布以中軍還魏。

translations.literal: Bu led the central army back to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Bu led the central guard back to Wei.

sentences.zh: 明日，會諸將議事，眾嘩曰：「公能行河朔舊事，則生死從公，不然，不可以戰。

translations.literal: The next day, meeting the generals to discuss affairs, the crowd clamored: "If you can follow the old ways of the Hebei commands, we live or die with you; otherwise we cannot fight."
translations.idiomatic: Next day at council the generals shouted: "Restore the old Hebei ways and we follow you to death—otherwise we will not fight."

sentences.zh: 」布度眾且亂，嘆曰：「功無成矣！

translations.literal: Bu judged the crowd would soon riot and sighed: "Merit will not be achieved!"
translations.idiomatic: Bu saw riot coming and sighed: "There is no victory here."

sentences.zh: 」即為書謝帝曰：「臣觀眾意，終且負國。

translations.literal: He then wrote a letter apologizing to the emperor: "Your servant sees the troops' intent—they will in the end betray the state.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the emperor: "I see the troops will betray the throne in the end.

sentences.zh: 臣無功，不敢忘死。

translations.literal: Your servant has no merit and dares not forget death.
translations.idiomatic: I have no merit, but I will not shrink from death.

sentences.zh: 願速救元翼，毋使忠臣義士塗炭於河朔。

translations.literal: I beg you quickly rescue Yuanji, and do not let loyal ministers and righteous soldiers be ruined in the Hebei."
translations.idiomatic: Hurry to save Yuanji—do not let loyal men be destroyed in Hebei."

sentences.zh: 」哭授其從事李石訖，乃入，至几筵，引刀刺心曰：「上以謝君父，下以示三軍。

translations.literal: Weeping, he handed it to his aide Li Shi to finish, then entered, went to the offering table, drew a knife and stabbed his heart, saying: "Above to apologize to lord and father, below to show the three armies."
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, he gave the letter to aide Li Shi, entered, stood at the altar, stabbed his heart, and said: "Above, to answer my emperor and father; below, to answer my army."

sentences.zh: 」言訖而絕，年三十八，贈尚書右僕射，謚曰孝。

translations.literal: When he finished speaking he died, age thirty-eight; posthumously granted Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, posthumous title Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-eight, posthumously made Right Vice Director with the posthumous name Xiao.

sentences.zh: 子鐬，宣宗時歷銀州刺史，坐以私鎧易邊馬論死，宰相崔鉉奏布死節於國，可貸鐬以勸忠烈，故貶為州司馬。

translations.literal: His son Huan, in Emperor Xuanzong's time successively served as prefect of Yin and, for exchanging private armor for frontier horses, was sentenced to death; Chief Minister Cui Xuan memorialized that Bu died for the state and Huan could be spared to encourage loyalty, so he was reduced to libationer in a prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Huan served as Yin prefect under Xuanzong and was condemned to death for trading private armor for frontier horses; Cui Xuan argued Bu had died for the state and Huan should be spared to honor loyalty, so he was reduced to prefectural libationer.

sentences.zh: 布弟 群群，會昌中歷蔡州刺史，坐贓且抵死，兄肇聞之，不食卒。

translations.literal: Bu's younger brother Qun—Qun, in Huichang served as prefect of Cai, was condemned to death for corruption; elder brother Zhao, hearing it, stopped eating and died.
