translations.idiomatic: Bu's brother Qun was Cai prefect in Huichang and was condemned to death for graft; his elder brother Zhao, hearing it, starved himself to death.

sentences.zh: 宰相李德裕奏：「漢河間人尹次、潁川人史玉坐殺人當死，次兄初、玉母渾詣官請代，因縊物故，於時皆赦其死。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Li Deyu memorialized: "In Han times Yin Ci of Hejian and Shi Yu of Yingchuan were condemned to death for murder; Ci's elder brother Chu and Yu's mother Hun went to the magistrate to take their place and died by hanging on the spot—at the time both were pardoned from death."
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu cited Han precedents: Yin Ci and Shi Yu faced death for murder; their kin offered to die in their place and were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 」於是武宗詔減死一等。

translations.literal: Thereupon Emperor Wuzong ordered the death penalty reduced one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong then reduced the sentence by one degree.

sentences.zh: 群弟 牟牟寬厚明吏治，為神策大將軍。

translations.literal: Qun's younger brother Mou—Mou was generous and understood governance, and served as great general of the Divine Strategy Army.
translations.idiomatic: Qun's brother Mou was generous and skilled in administration, and became a great general of the Divine Strategy Army.

sentences.zh: 開成初，鹽州刺史王宰失羌人之和，詔牟代之。

translations.literal: At the start of Kaicheng, Prefect Wang Zai of Yan lost harmony with the Qiang; an edict ordered Mou replace him.
translations.idiomatic: In early Kaicheng Yan prefect Wang Zai lost the Qiang's trust; Mou replaced him.

sentences.zh: 累遷鄜坊節度使，再徙天平，三為武寧，一為靈武軍，官至檢校尚書左僕射，卒。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to military governor of Bian and Fang, then twice transferred to Tianping, three times to Wuning, once to Lingwu, reaching Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Bian-Fang governor, served twice at Tianping, three times at Wuning, once at Lingwu, reached acting Left Vice Director, and died.

sentences.zh: 諸子皆有方面功，以忠義為當世所高。

translations.literal: All the sons had merit in their regions and were honored by the age for loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Every son won regional distinction, and the age honored the family for loyalty.

sentences.zh: = 王承元 =

translations.literal: = Wang Chengyuan =
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengyuan

sentences.zh: 王承元者，承宗弟也。

translations.literal: Wang Chengyuan was Chengzong's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengyuan was the younger brother of Chengzong.

sentences.zh: 有沈謀。

translations.literal: He had deep stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: He was deeply shrewd.

sentences.zh: 年十六，勸承宗亟引兵共討李師道，承宗少之，不用，然軍中往往指目之。

translations.literal: At sixteen he urged Chengzong to lead troops promptly to join in attacking Li Shidao; Chengzong thought him young and did not use [the advice], yet in the army people often pointed at him.
translations.idiomatic: At sixteen he urged Chengzong to march against Li Shidao; Chengzong dismissed him as young, but the troops watched him closely.

sentences.zh: 承宗死，未發喪，大將謀取帥它姓。

translations.literal: When Chengzong died, before the mourning was announced, the great generals plotted to take the command for another surname.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengzong died, before mourning was announced, senior generals plotted to give the command to another clan.

sentences.zh: 參謀崔燧與諸校計，以祖母涼國夫人李命承元嗣。

translations.literal: Staff officer Cui Sui and the commanders planned, and by order of Grandmother, Lady Li of Liang, had Chengyuan succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Staff officer Cui Sui and the commanders arranged for Grandmother Lady Li of Liang to name Chengyuan successor.

sentences.zh: 承元泣且拜，不受，諸將牢請，承元曰：「上使中貴人監軍，盍先請？

translations.literal: Chengyuan wept and bowed, refusing; the generals firmly pressed him; Chengyuan said: "The throne sends palace eunuchs to supervise the army—had we not better ask first?"
translations.idiomatic: Chengyuan wept and refused; the generals pressed him. He said: "The court sends eunuch supervisors—should we not ask them first?"

sentences.zh: 」監軍至，又如命，乃謝曰：「諸君不忘王氏以及孺子，茍有令，其從我乎？

translations.literal: When the supervisor arrived and again gave the order, he then thanked them, saying: "You do not forget the Wang house and this child—if there is a command, will you follow me?"
translations.idiomatic: When the supervisor confirmed the order, he thanked them: "You remember the Wang house and this boy—if I command, will you obey?"

sentences.zh: 」眾曰：「惟所命。

translations.literal: The crowd said: "As you command."
translations.idiomatic: "Whatever you say," they answered.

sentences.zh: 」乃視事牙闔之偏，約左右不得稱留後，事一關參佐，密表請帥於朝。

translations.literal: He then conducted affairs at the side gate of headquarters, stipulating that those around him must not call him acting governor; every matter went through staff; secretly he memorialized requesting a court-appointed governor.
translations.idiomatic: He took office at a side gate, forbade the title "acting governor," routed all business through staff, and secretly asked the court for a appointed commander.

sentences.zh: 穆宗詔起居舍人柏耆宣慰。

translations.literal: Muzong ordered Palace Diarist Bai Qi to proclaim consolation.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong sent Palace Diarist Bai Qi to announce imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 授承元檢校工部尚書、義成軍節度使。

translations.literal: Chengyuan was appointed Acting Minister of Works and military governor of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyuan was made acting Minister of Works and governor of Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 北鎮以兩河故事脅誘，承元不納，諸將皆悔。

translations.literal: The northern garrisons coerced and tempted him with the two-river precedent; Chengyuan would not accept, and the generals all regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Northern commands tempted him with old two-river precedents; he refused, and his generals regretted it.

sentences.zh: 耆至，士哭於軍，承元令曰：「諸君不欲我去，意固善。

translations.literal: When Qi arrived the soldiers wept in camp; Chengyuan ordered: "You do not wish me to leave—your intent is indeed good.
translations.idiomatic: When Bai Qi arrived the troops wept. Chengyuan said: "You want me to stay—that is kind.

sentences.zh: 雖然，格天子詔，我獲罪奈何？

translations.literal: Even so, if we resist the Son of Heaven's edict, how can I escape guilt?"
translations.idiomatic: But if we defy the emperor's edict, how do I answer for it?"

sentences.zh: 前李師道有詔赦死，欲舉族西，諸將止弗遣，他日乃共殺之。

translations.literal: Formerly Li Shidao had an edict pardoning him from death; he wished to move his whole clan west, but the generals stopped and would not let him go—later they jointly killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shidao once had a pardon and tried to move his clan west; his generals stopped him—and later killed him.

sentences.zh: 今君等幸置我，無與師道比。

translations.literal: Now you are fortunate to release me—do not compare me with Shidao."
translations.idiomatic: Be generous and let me go—do not make me another Shidao."

sentences.zh: 」乃遍拜諸將，諸將語塞。

translations.literal: He then bowed to every general in turn; the generals were speechless.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed to each general in turn; none could answer.

sentences.zh: 承元即出家貲盡賜之，斬不從命者十輩，軍乃定。

translations.literal: Chengyuan then took his family wealth and gave it all away, beheaded ten who would not obey orders, and the army then settled.
translations.idiomatic: He gave away his family fortune, executed ten who disobeyed, and the army settled.

sentences.zh: 於是諫議大夫鄭覃宣慰，賜其軍錢百萬緡，赦囚徒，問孤獨、廢疾不能自存者粟帛有差。

translations.literal: Thereupon Remonstrance Officer Zheng Tan proclaimed consolation, bestowing on the army one million strings of cash, pardoning prisoners, and inquiring after orphans, the alone, and the disabled who could not support themselves with grain and cloth in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Officer Zheng Tan announced imperial grace: a million strings for the army, amnesty for prisoners, and relief for orphans, the alone, and the disabled.

sentences.zh: 承元去鎮，左右裒器幣自隨，承元使空褚毋留。

translations.literal: When Chengyuan left his post, attendants gathered vessels and goods to take along; Chengyuan had the chests emptied and nothing kept.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving command, attendants packed valuables to carry off; Chengyuan emptied every chest and took nothing.

sentences.zh: 入朝，昆弟拜刺史者四人，位於朝者四十人。

translations.literal: Entering court, four brothers were appointed prefects and forty kinsmen held court rank.
translations.idiomatic: At court four brothers were made prefects and forty kinsmen held office.

sentences.zh: 祖母入見，帝命中宮禮賚異等。

translations.literal: Grandmother entered audience; the emperor ordered the empress to receive her with exceptional ceremonial gifts.
translations.idiomatic: His grandmother was received in audience; the empress was ordered to honor her with special gifts.

sentences.zh: 徙承元鄜坊丹延節度。

translations.literal: Chengyuan was transferred to military governor of Bian, Fang, Dan, and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Chengyuan was transferred to governor of Bian, Fang, Dan, and Yan.

sentences.zh: 俄徙鳳翔。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he moved to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔右袤涇、原，地平少巖險，吐蕃數入盜。

translations.literal: Fengxiang bordered Jing and Yuan on the right; the land was flat with little cliff defense, and Tibetans repeatedly entered to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxiang bordered Jing and Yuan on a flat plain with little natural defense, and Tibetans raided often.

sentences.zh: 承元據勝地為鄣，置守兵千，詔號臨汧城。

translations.literal: Chengyuan seized favorable ground for a barrier fort, posted one thousand guard troops, and an edict named it Linqian city.
translations.idiomatic: He built a barrier fort on strong ground, garrisoned a thousand men, and the court named it Linqian.

sentences.zh: 府郛左百賈州聚，異時為虜剽奪，至燎烽相警，承元版堞繚之，人乃告安。

translations.literal: To the left of headquarters a hundred merchants gathered from the prefectures; in other times barbarians plundered them, until beacon fires warned one another; Chengyuan walled and encircled it, and people then reported peace.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants from a hundred districts gathered west of headquarters and were often robbed until beacon fires lined the roads; Chengyuan walled the market and people slept safely.

sentences.zh: 以勞封岐國公。

translations.literal: For the labor he was enfeoffed Duke of Qi state.
translations.idiomatic: For the work he was enfeoffed Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 太和初，祖母喪，詔曰：「武俊當橫流時，拯定奔潰，功在史官。

translations.literal: At the start of Taihe, grandmother died; an edict said: "Wujun, in the time of rushing currents, stabilized the fleeing and collapsing—merit recorded in the histories.
translations.idiomatic: In early Taihe his grandmother died; an edict said: "Wujun, in turbulent times, steadied the fleeing collapse—merit written in the histories.

sentences.zh: 今李不幸，贈恤宜加厚。

translations.literal: Now Lady Li has died untimely; posthumous favor should be thick."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li's death is untimely; posthumous honors should be generous."

sentences.zh: 」且給儀仗以葬。

translations.literal: Moreover ceremonial guards were granted for the burial.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial guards were sent for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 五年，徙節平盧、淄青。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was transferred to military governor of Pinglu and Ziqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was posted governor of Pinglu and Ziqing.

sentences.zh: 始，鹽禁未嘗行兩河，承元請歸有司，由是兗、鄆諸鎮皆奉法。

translations.literal: At first the salt monopoly had never been enforced in the two Hebei commands; Chengyuan requested it return to the proper offices, and thereby Yan, Yun, and the other garrisons all obeyed the law.
translations.idiomatic: The salt monopoly had never applied in Hebei; Chengyuan returned it to central control, and Yan, Yun, and the other commands followed suit.

sentences.zh: 承元資仁裕，所至愛利。

translations.literal: Chengyuan was generous and magnanimous by nature; wherever he went he loved and benefited the people.
translations.idiomatic: Generous by nature, he governed wherever he went with care for the people.

sentences.zh: 卒，年三十三，贈司徒。

translations.literal: He died at age thirty-three; posthumously granted Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died at thirty-three and was posthumously made Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: = 牛元翼 =

translations.literal: = Niu Yuanji =
translations.idiomatic: Niu Yuanji

sentences.zh: 牛元翼，趙州人。

translations.literal: Niu Yuanji was a man of Zhao prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Yuanji was from Zhao prefecture.

sentences.zh: 材果而謀。

translations.literal: He had talent and resolution in planning.
translations.idiomatic: He was bold and resourceful.

sentences.zh: 王承宗時倚其計為強雄，與傅良弼二人冠諸將。

translations.literal: Under Wang Chengzong he relied on his plans as a strong champion; with Fu Liangbi the two stood above all the generals.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wang Chengzong he was the strongest strategist; with Fu Liangbi he ranked above every general.

sentences.zh: 王廷湊叛，穆宗以元翼在成德，名出廷湊遠甚，自深州刺史擢為深冀節度使，以攜其軍。

translations.literal: When Wang Tingcou rebelled, Muzong, because Yuanji was in Chengde and his fame far exceeded Tingcou's, promoted him from prefect of Shen to military governor of Shen and Ji to divide their army.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Tingcou rebelled, Muzong promoted Yuanji from Shen prefect to governor of Shen and Ji—his fame in Chengde far outshone Tingcou's, and the court meant to split the army.

sentences.zh: 廷湊怒，遣部將王位以銳兵攻元翼，不勝，乃合朱克融共圍之。

translations.literal: Tingcou was enraged and sent his subordinate general Wang Wei with crack troops to attack Yuanji; he did not prevail, and therefore joined Zhu Kerong to besiege him together.
translations.idiomatic: Tingcou sent general Wang Wei with elite troops against Yuanji; failing, he joined Zhu Kerong in a joint siege.

sentences.zh: 詔進元翼成德軍節度使，以宣武兵五百進援，元翼固守。

translations.literal: An edict promoted Yuanji to military governor of Chengde and sent five hundred Xuanwu troops as advance relief; Yuanji held firm.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Yuanji governor of Chengde and sent five hundred Xuanwu troops to reinforce him; he held out.

sentences.zh: 長慶二年，詔赦廷湊罪，徙元翼山南東道，以深州賜廷湊，使中人促元翼南。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changqing an edict pardoned Tingcou's crime, transferred Yuanji to Shannan East Circuit, granted Shen prefecture to Tingcou, and sent palace eunuchs to hurry Yuanji south.
translations.idiomatic: In Changqing 2 the court pardoned Tingcou, moved Yuanji to Shannan East, gave Shenzhou to Tingcou, and sent eunuchs to hurry Yuanji south.

sentences.zh: 廷湊恨之，已受詔，兵不解。

translations.literal: Tingcou hated this; though he had received the edict, his troops did not stand down.
translations.idiomatic: Tingcou hated the deal; though he accepted the edict, his siege never lifted.

sentences.zh: 招討使裴度詒書誚讓，克融解而歸，廷湊退舍。

translations.literal: Campaign commander Pei Du sent a letter reproaching and blaming; Kerong withdrew and returned, and Tingcou pulled back his camp.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign commander Pei Du rebuked them in writing; Kerong withdrew and Tingcou pulled back.

sentences.zh: 詔並加檢校工部尚書，兩悅之。

translations.literal: An edict additionally made both Acting Ministers of Works, pleasing both.
translations.idiomatic: Both were made acting Ministers of Works, and both were mollified.

sentences.zh: 淹月，元翼率十餘騎冒圍跳德、棣，朝京師。

translations.literal: After a full month Yuanji led more than ten horsemen to break the encirclement, leap to De and Di, and attend court in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: A month later Yuanji broke out with a dozen horsemen, rode to De and Di, and reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 廷湊入，盡殺元翼親將臧平等百八十人。

translations.literal: Tingcou entered and killed Yuanji's close generals Zang Ping and one hundred eighty others.
translations.idiomatic: Tingcou entered and slaughtered Yuanji's chief officers, including Zang Ping—one hundred eighty men.

sentences.zh: 元翼見延英，賚問優縟，命中人楊再昌取其家，並迎田弘正喪。

translations.literal: Yuanji was received at Yanying; questions and gifts were lavish; the emperor ordered Palace Eunuch Yang Zaichang fetch his household and also bring Tian Hongzheng's coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji was received at Yanying with lavish honors; the emperor sent eunuch Yang Zaichang for his family and Tian Hongzheng's coffin.

sentences.zh: 廷湊辭以弘正殯亡在所，元翼家須秋遣。

translations.literal: Tingcou declined, saying Hongzheng's bier was wherever it lay; Yuanji's household would be sent in autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Tingcou refused, saying Hongzheng's coffin was wherever it happened to be and Yuanji's family would come in autumn.

sentences.zh: 魏博節度使史憲誠遣其弟入趙，四返，說廷湊曰：「田公非得罪於趙，屍尚何惜？

translations.literal: Wei Bo military governor Shi Xiancheng sent his younger brother into Zhao; four times he returned and persuaded Tingcou: "Minister Tian did not offend Zhao—why begrudge his corpse?
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bo governor Shi Xiancheng sent his brother into Zhao four times to tell Tingcou: "Minister Tian did Zhao no wrong—why withhold his body?

sentences.zh: 元翼去深州，乃一孤將，何利其家？

translations.literal: Yuanji has left Shen prefecture—he is a lone general; what profit in his household?"
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji has left Shenzhou—a lone general. What do you gain by holding his family?"

sentences.zh: 」廷湊乃歸弘正喪於京師。

translations.literal: Tingcou then returned Hongzheng's coffin to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Tingcou then sent Hongzheng's coffin to the capital.

sentences.zh: 元翼聞平等死，憤恚卒，悉還所賜於朝，廷湊遂夷其家。

translations.literal: Yuanji, hearing Ping and the others were dead, died of rage and indignation; he returned all the court's gifts, and Tingcou then exterminated his household.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanji died of rage when he learned Ping and the rest were dead; he sent back every court gift, and Tingcou wiped out his family.

sentences.zh: 附 傅良弼良弼字安道，清河人。

translations.literal: Appendix: Fu Liangbi—Liangbi, style name Andao, was a man of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Fu Liangbi, courtesy name Andao, was from Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 以射冠軍中。

translations.literal: With archery he stood first in the army.
translations.idiomatic: He was the army's finest archer.

sentences.zh: 初，瀛之博野、樂壽，介范陽、成德間，每兵交，先薄二城，故常為劇屯。

translations.literal: At first Boye and Yueshou in Ying lay between Fanyang and Chengde; whenever armies clashed they first pressed the two cities, so they were always critical garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Boye and Yueshou in Ying lay between Fanyang and Chengde; every campaign struck them first, so both were critical posts.

sentences.zh: 德宗以王武俊破朱滔功，皆隸成德，故以良弼守樂壽，李寰守博野。

translations.literal: Emperor Dezong, because Wang Wujun had merit breaking Zhu Tao, both were placed under Chengde; therefore Liangbi was made to hold Yueshou and Li Huan to hold Boye.
translations.idiomatic: Dezong placed both under Chengde after Wang Wujun broke Zhu Tao; Liangbi held Yueshou and Li Huan held Boye.

sentences.zh: 廷湊之叛，兩賊交誘之，而堅壁為國固守。

translations.literal: When Tingcou rebelled, both bandits alternately tempted them, yet they held their walls and steadfastly guarded for the state.
translations.idiomatic: When Tingcou rebelled both rebels tried to win them, but they held their walls for the throne.

sentences.zh: 有詔以樂壽為左神策行營，拜良弼為都知兵馬使；

translations.literal: An edict made Yueshou the Left Divine Strategy mobile camp and appointed Liangbi commander knowing army and horse affairs;
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Yueshou the Left Divine Strategy mobile camp and named Liangbi its army commander;

sentences.zh: 寰所領士隸右神策，號忻州營，亦以寰為都知兵馬使。

translations.literal: the troops Huan led were placed under the Right Divine Strategy, titled Xinzhou camp, and Huan too was made commander knowing army and horse affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Huan's troops joined the Right Divine Strategy as the Xinzhou camp, with Huan as commander.

sentences.zh: 賜第京師。

translations.literal: Residences in the capital were granted.
translations.idiomatic: They were given houses in the capital.

sentences.zh: 俄以良弼為沂州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon Liangbi was appointed prefect of Yi prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon named prefect of Yi.

sentences.zh: 良弼率眾出，戰力，乃得去。

translations.literal: Liangbi led the crowd out, fought hard, and only then got away.
translations.idiomatic: Liangbi fought his way out with his men and barely escaped.

sentences.zh: 寰引兵三千趨忻州，廷湊邀之，寰斬三百級，追者不敢前。

translations.literal: Huan led three thousand troops toward Xin prefecture; Tingcou intercepted him; Huan beheaded three hundred at the head and the pursuers did not dare advance.
translations.idiomatic: Huan marched three thousand men toward Xinzhou; Tingcou intercepted him; Huan killed three hundred pursuers and the rest halted.

sentences.zh: 天子以良弼、寰忠有狀，乃更賜奴婢服馬。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven, because Liangbi and Huan had shown loyalty, then further bestowed slaves, maids, robes, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rewarded their loyalty with slaves, maids, robes, and horses.

sentences.zh: 召良弼為左神策軍將軍。

translations.literal: Liangbi was summoned as general of the Left Divine Strategy Army.
translations.idiomatic: Liangbi was recalled as general of the Left Divine Strategy Army.

sentences.zh: 寶歷初，擢夏綏銀節度使。

translations.literal: At the start of Baoli he was promoted to military governor of Xia, Sui, and Yin.
translations.idiomatic: In early Baoli he became governor of Xia, Sui, and Yin.

sentences.zh: 異時蕃帳亡命來者，必償馬乃與，良弼至，皆執付其部，酋種歡懷。

translations.literal: In other times when tribal tents sent fugitives, horses had to be paid before they were accepted; when Liangbi arrived, all were seized and delivered to their tribes; chieftains rejoiced in trust.
translations.idiomatic: Former governors demanded payment for every tribal refugee; Liangbi seized fugitives and returned them to their tribes, and the chiefs trusted him.

sentences.zh: 終橫海節度使。

translations.literal: He ended as military governor of Heng and Hai.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as governor of Heng-Hai.

sentences.zh: 寰擢累保義軍節度使。

translations.literal: Huan was promoted cumulatively to military governor of Baoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Huan rose to governor of Baoyi.

sentences.zh: 王智興討李同捷未克，而烏重胤卒，謂寰可共立功，請諸朝，乃授橫海節度使。

translations.literal: Wang Zhixing had not yet overcome Li Tongjie when Wu Chongyin died; he said Huan could share in achieving merit and requested him of the court; thereupon he was granted military governor of Heng and Hai.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhixing, failing against Li Tongjie after Wu Chongyin died, asked the court for Huan as co-commander and got him as Heng-Hai governor.

sentences.zh: 師所過暴鈔，至屯，按軍不進，遂身入朝，盛陳賊勢，請濟師，欲大調發。

translations.literal: Wherever the army passed it plundered violently; arriving at camp, it inspected the army and did not advance; he then entered court in person, greatly stating the bandits' strength, requesting reinforcements, wishing for a great mobilization.
translations.idiomatic: His army looted every march and stalled at camp; he went to court in person, overstated the enemy, and demanded massive reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 群臣議寰兵太重，且盜滄、景，未決而棣州平。

translations.literal: The ministers debated that Huan's army was too heavy and also plundered Cang and Jing; undecided, Di prefecture was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers feared Huan's army was too large and was raiding Cang and Jing; before they decided, Di prefecture fell.

sentences.zh: 寰內愧不自安，願留京師，遂罷保義軍、忻州營，更授夏綏宥節度使，卒。

translations.literal: Huan inwardly felt ashamed and ill at ease, wished to remain in the capital, and therefore Baoyi army and Xinzhou camp were abolished; he was again granted military governor of Xia, Sui, and You, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, Huan asked to stay at court; Baoyi and the Xinzhou camp were dissolved; he was reposted to Xia-Sui-You and died.

sentences.zh: 寰再易鎮，治無可言者。

translations.literal: Huan changed commands twice; in governance there was nothing to speak of.
translations.idiomatic: After two transfers his governance amounted to little.

sentences.zh: 然廷湊之亂，聯軍十五萬無成功，賊鋒不可嬰，而樂壽、博野截然峙中者累歲，梗其吞暴，議者以為難。

translations.literal: Yet in Tingcou's rebellion, the allied armies of one hundred fifty thousand achieved no success—the bandits' edge could not be touched—while Yueshou and Boye stood sharply apart in the midst for years, blocking their swallowing violence; debaters considered it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Yet while a hundred fifty thousand allied troops failed against Tingcou, Yueshou and Boye stood alone in the middle for years and blocked his expansion—no small feat, debaters said.

sentences.zh: 敬宗世，寰圖其事上之。

translations.literal: In Emperor Jingzong's time Huan mapped the affair and submitted it upward.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jingzong, Huan mapped the campaign and submitted it to the throne.

sentences.zh: = 史孝章 =

translations.literal: = Shi Xiaozhang =
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiaozhang

sentences.zh: 史孝章，字得仁，資修謹。

translations.literal: Shi Xiaozhang, style name Deren, was by nature cultivated and careful.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Xiaozhang, courtesy name Deren, was careful and cultivated.

sentences.zh: 父憲誠，以戰力奮，賓客用挽強擊劍相矜，孝章獨退讓如諸生，稱道皆《詩》、《書》。

translations.literal: His father Xiancheng, through fighting strength, rose; guests used drawing the bow and swordplay to boast to one another—Xiaozhang alone yielded like a student and in conversation cited only the Odes and Documents.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xiancheng rose by force; guests bragged of archery and swordplay—Xiaozhang hung back like a scholar and quoted only the Odes and Documents.

sentences.zh: 魏博節度使李訴閱大將子弟籍於軍，孝章願以文署職，奇之，檄試都督府參軍。

translations.literal: Wei Bo military governor Li Su reviewed the register of great generals' sons and nephews in the army; Xiaozhang wished to take a literary post; Su marveled and ordered a trial as adjutant of the governor's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bo governor Li Su reviewed officers' sons on the rolls; Xiaozhang asked for a civil post; Su was impressed and tested him as headquarters adjutant.

sentences.zh: 憲誠得魏，遷士曹參軍。

translations.literal: When Xiancheng obtained Wei, he was transferred to army personnel adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiancheng took Wei, Xiaozhang became army personnel adjutant.

sentences.zh: 孝章見父數奸命，內非之，承間諫曰：「大河之北號富強，然而挺亂取地，天下指河朔若夷狄然。

translations.literal: Xiaozhang saw his father repeatedly defying orders and inwardly disapproved; seizing an opening he remonstrated: "North of the great river is called rich and strong, yet by rising in disorder and seizing land, the realm points at Hebei as at barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his father repeatedly defy the throne, Xiaozhang urged him: "Hebei is called rich and strong, yet by seizing land in rebellion the empire treats us like barbarians.

sentences.zh: 今大人身封侯，家富不貲，非痛洗溉，竭節事上，恐吾踵不旋禍且至。

translations.literal: Now the elder is enfeoffed a marquis and the household wealth is beyond counting—unless you scour and wash yourself and exhaust loyalty serving the throne, I fear before my heel turns calamity will arrive."
translations.idiomatic: You are a marquis and our house overflows with wealth—unless you purge this and serve the throne utterly, disaster will come before I turn away."

sentences.zh: 」因涕下沾衿。

translations.literal: He wept until his collar was soaked.
translations.idiomatic: He wept until his collar was wet.

sentences.zh: 父粗武，不盡聽。

translations.literal: His father was rough and martial and did not fully listen.
translations.idiomatic: His rough-spirited father did not fully heed him.

sentences.zh: 文宗賢之，擢孝章節度副使，累遷檢校左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong admired him and promoted Xiaozhang deputy military commissioner, successively transferred to Acting Left Regular Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong admired him, made him deputy commissioner, and promoted him to acting Left Regular Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 父欲助李同捷，孝章切爭，憲誠稍憚其義。

translations.literal: His father wished to aid Li Tongjie; Xiaozhang argued fiercely; Xiancheng slightly feared his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When his father wanted to aid Li Tongjie, Xiaozhang argued fiercely and Xiancheng feared his integrity.

sentences.zh: 又勸出師討同捷自明，帝益嘉之，進檢校工部尚書。

translations.literal: He also urged sending troops to attack Tongjie to clarify himself; the emperor further praised him and promoted Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He urged marching against Tongjie to prove loyalty; the emperor praised him and made him acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 及兵出，父敕孝章統之。

translations.literal: When the army marched out, his father ordered Xiaozhang to command it.
translations.idiomatic: When the army marched, his father put Xiaozhang in command.

sentences.zh: 入朝，勞予蕃厚。

translations.literal: Entering court, he was consoled and rewarded with thick gifts.
translations.idiomatic: At court he was honored with rich rewards.

sentences.zh: 憲誠亦上書求覲，帝知非憲誠意，特緣孝章悟發，故分相、衛、澶而授孝章節度使。

translations.literal: Xiancheng also submitted a memorial requesting audience; the emperor knew it was not Xiancheng's intent but specially because Xiaozhang's understanding had awakened; therefore Xiang, Wei, and Chan were divided off and Xiaozhang was granted military governorship.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng asked to come to court; the emperor knew the idea was Xiaozhang's, not his, and split off Xiang, Wei, and Chan for Xiaozhang as governor.

sentences.zh: 未至，魏人亂，父卒死於軍。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, the people of Wei rioted and his father died suddenly in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Before he arrived Wei mutinied and his father died in camp.

sentences.zh: 帝念史氏禍而恤孝章，故奪喪拜右金吾衛將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor, mindful of the Shi house's calamity and pitying Xiaozhang, therefore seized mourning and appointed Right Golden Guard general.
translations.idiomatic: Pitying Xiaozhang amid the Shi disaster, the emperor cut short mourning and made him Right Golden Guard general.

sentences.zh: 徙節鄜坊，進檢校戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to military governor of Bian and Fang and promoted to Acting Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to Bian-Fang and promoted to acting Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 久之，自邠寧以病丐還，卒於行，年三十九，贈尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: After a long time, from Binning he requested return on grounds of illness and died on the road at age thirty-nine; posthumously granted Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Long after, he left Binning ill, died on the road at thirty-nine, and was posthumously made Right Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 孝章本名唐，後改今名。

translations.literal: Xiaozhang's original name was Tang; later it was changed to the present name.
translations.idiomatic: He was originally named Tang and later renamed Xiaozhang.

sentences.zh: 從父 憲誠憲誠弟憲忠，字元貞，少為魏牙門將。

translations.literal: Paternal uncle Xiancheng—Xiancheng's younger brother Xianzhong, style name Yuanzhen, in youth was a Wei gate general.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng's younger brother Xianzhong, courtesy name Yuanzhen, was a Wei gate general in youth.

sentences.zh: 田弘正討齊、蔡，常為先鋒，閱三十戰，中流矢，酣鬥不解，由是著名。

translations.literal: When Tian Hongzheng attacked Qi and Cai he was always vanguard; through thirty battles he took arrows in the stream yet fought on without slackening, and thereby became famous.
translations.idiomatic: In Tian Hongzheng's campaigns against Qi and Cai he always led the van; in thirty battles he kept fighting though arrows struck him, and fame followed.

sentences.zh: 憲誠表為貝州刺史。

translations.literal: Xiancheng memorialized appointing him prefect of Bei.
translations.idiomatic: Xiancheng had him appointed prefect of Bei.

sentences.zh: 魏亂，奔京師，加累檢校右散騎常侍、隴州刺史。

translations.literal: When Wei fell into disorder he fled to the capital and was additionally made cumulatively Acting Right Regular Palace Attendant and prefect of Long.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei rebelled he fled to court and was made acting Right Regular Palace Attendant and Long prefect.

sentences.zh: 增亭鄣，徙客館於外，戎諜無所伺。

translations.literal: He added barrier forts and moved guest lodges outside; barbarian spies had nowhere to watch.
translations.idiomatic: He added outposts and moved guest lodges outside the walls so enemy spies could not watch.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，築三原城，吐蕃因之數犯邊。

translations.literal: In Huichang he built Sanyuan city; Tibetans therefore repeatedly violated the border.
translations.idiomatic: In Huichang he built Sanyuan city; Tibetans raided the border more often because of it.

sentences.zh: 拜憲忠涇原節度使以怖其侵，吐蕃遣使來請墮城，且願以嘗殺使者之人置塞上。

translations.literal: Xianzhong was appointed military governor of Jingyuan to intimidate their raids; Tibet sent envoys requesting the city be demolished and wished to place on the frontier the men who had once killed their envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong was made Jingyuan governor to deter raids; Tibet asked that Sanyuan be razed and demanded the men who had killed their envoys be handed over.

sentences.zh: 憲忠使謝曰：「前吾未城。

translations.literal: Xianzhong sent thanks, saying: "Formerly I had not built the city.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong replied: "Before I built the city,

sentences.zh: 爾犯我地，安得禁吾城？

translations.literal: You violated my territory—how can you forbid my building a city?"
translations.idiomatic: you crossed my land. How can you forbid me to build?"

sentences.zh: 爾知殺吾使為負，宜先取罪人謝我，將無所不得。

translations.literal: You know that killing my envoy was wrong—you should first take the guilty and apologize to me; then nothing will be refused.
translations.idiomatic: "You know killing my envoy was wrong—bring the guilty and apologize first; then we can talk of anything.

sentences.zh: 今與爾約，前節度使事一置之。

translations.literal: Now I make a pact with you—the former military governor's affair is set aside entirely."
translations.idiomatic: Today I offer a pact: forget what the last governor did."

sentences.zh: 」吐蕃情得而服。

translations.literal: The Tibetans' feelings were satisfied and they submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Tibet was satisfied and submitted.

sentences.zh: 憲忠疏涇於隍，積緡錢十萬、粟百萬斛，戍人宜之。

translations.literal: Xianzhong dredged the Jing moat, accumulated one hundred thousand strings of cash and one million hu of grain; the garrison troops found it suitable.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged Jingzhou's moat, stockpiled a hundred thousand strings and a million hu of grain, and the garrison approved.

sentences.zh: 會党項羌內寇，又徙朔方，有詔馳驛赴屯，憲忠辭曰：「羌不得其心，故不自安。

translations.literal: When the Tangut Qiang raided inward, he was again transferred to Shuofang; an edict ordered post relay to hurry to garrison; Xianzhong declined, saying: "The Qiang do not have their hearts settled, therefore they are not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: When Tangut Qiang raided inland he was transferred to Shuofang; ordered to rush by relay, Xianzhong refused: "The Qiang are unsettled and restless.

sentences.zh: 今亟往，知吾為備，鬥益健，請徐行。

translations.literal: If I go now in haste, knowing I am prepared they will fight all the harder—I request to go slowly."
translations.idiomatic: If I hurry now they will know we are ready and fight harder—I ask to march slowly."

sentences.zh: 」許之。

translations.literal: It was granted.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃移書與羌人，示要約。

translations.literal: He then sent letters to the Qiang showing terms and covenants.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the Qiang letters setting terms.

sentences.zh: 羌人乃皆喜，奉酒湩迎道。

translations.literal: The Qiang then all rejoiced, offering wine and kumiss along the road to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang rejoiced and met him on the road with wine and kumiss.

sentences.zh: 大中初，突厥擾河東，鈔漕米行賈，徙節振武軍。

translations.literal: At the start of Dazhong, Turks harassed Hedong and plundered transport grain and traveling merchants; he was transferred to military governor of Zhenwu.
translations.idiomatic: In early Dazhong Turks harassed Hedong and looted grain convoys and merchants; he was posted to Zhenwu.

sentences.zh: 於是故帥荒沓，使遊弈兵覘戎有良馬牛，強取之，歸直十一，戎人怒，因興盜掠。

translations.literal: There the former governor was negligent and disorderly; he sent roaming patrol soldiers to scout the barbarians for good horses and cattle and forcibly took them, paying one in ten on return—the barbarians were enraged and therefore began raiding.
translations.idiomatic: The previous governor had been slack; patrols scouted tribal herds and seized good horses and cattle, paying a tenth of value—the tribes raged and raided.

sentences.zh: 憲忠廉儉，少所欲，嘗曰：「吾居河朔，去此三千里，乃乘五健馬。

translations.literal: Xianzhong was incorrupt and frugal with few desires; he once said: "When I dwelt in Hebei, three thousand li from here, I rode five strong horses.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal and upright, he said: "In Hebei, three thousand li from here, I rode five good horses.

sentences.zh: 今守邊，發吾余奉，不患無馬，何忍豪市哉？

translations.literal: Now guarding the frontier, spending my surplus salary, I do not fear lacking horses—how can I bear to buy them by force?"
translations.idiomatic: Now on the frontier I live on my salary and lack no horses—how could I seize them by force?"

sentences.zh: 」故所至莫不懷德。

translations.literal: Therefore wherever he went none did not cherish his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served, men honored his integrity.

sentences.zh: 累封北海縣子，檢校尚書左僕射，兼金吾大將軍。

translations.literal: Through cumulative enfeoffments he was made Viscount of Beihai, Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and concurrent great general of the Golden Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed Viscount of Beihai, made acting Left Vice Director, and concurrent Golden Guard general.

sentences.zh: 以病自丐，改左龍武統軍。

translations.literal: Ill, he requested on his own behalf and was changed to commander of the Left Dragon Martial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Ill, he asked to retire and was made commander of the Left Dragon Martial Guard.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十一，贈司空。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-one; posthumously granted Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-one and was posthumously made Minister of Works.
